translations.literal: Volume 217
translations.idiomatic: Volume 217

sentences.zh: 【唐紀三十三】 起閼逢敦牂，盡柔兆涒灘四月，凡二年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 33] From Yanmen Dunzang through the fourth month of Rouzhao Youtan; a little more than two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 33] From Yanmen Dunzang through the fourth month of Rouzhao Youtan—a little more than two years in all.

sentences.zh: 玄宗至道大聖大明孝皇帝下之下天寶十三年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong of Tang, Latter Part of the Lower Scroll, Tianbao year 13 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong of Tang, Latter Part of the Lower Scroll, Tianbao year 13 (

sentences.zh: 甲午，公元七五四年）

translations.literal: jiawu, AD 754)
translations.idiomatic: jiawu, AD 754)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己亥，安祿山入朝。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on yihai, An Lushan came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on yihai, An Lushan came to court.

sentences.zh: 是時楊國忠言祿山必反，且曰：「陛下試召之，必不來。」

translations.literal: At this time Yang Guozhong said An Lushan would surely rebel, and further said, "Your Majesty, try summoning him—he will certainly not come."
translations.idiomatic: At this time Yang Guozhong insisted that An Lushan would surely rebel, and said, "Your Majesty, try summoning him—he will certainly not come."

sentences.zh: 上使召之，祿山聞命即至。

translations.literal: The emperor sent to summon him; Lushan, on hearing the order, came at once.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent to summon him; on hearing the order, Lushan came at once.

sentences.zh: 庚子，見上於華清宮，泣曰：「臣本胡人，陛下寵擢至此，為國忠所疾，臣死無日矣！」

translations.literal: On gengzi he saw the emperor at Huaqing Palace and wept, saying, "Your servant is originally a barbarian; Your Majesty favored and promoted me to this point, yet Guozhong resents me—I have not long to live!"
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi he saw the emperor at Huaqing Palace and wept, saying, "I am only a foreigner whom Your Majesty raised to such heights; Guozhong hates me for it—I may die any day now!"

sentences.zh: 上憐之，賞賜巨萬，由是益親信祿山，國忠之言不能入矣。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied him and bestowed rewards worth tens of thousands; from this he trusted Lushan all the more, and Guozhong's words could no longer gain entry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took pity on him and lavished rewards worth tens of thousands of strings of cash; from then on he trusted Lushan all the more, and Guozhong's warnings could no longer get through.

sentences.zh: 太子亦知祿山必反，言於上，上不聽。

translations.literal: The crown prince also knew Lushan would rebel and spoke to the emperor; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince too knew Lushan would rebel and told the emperor, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，太清宮奏：「學士李琪見玄元皇帝乘紫雲，告以國祚延昌。」

translations.literal: On jiachen the Supreme Ultimate Palace reported: "Academician Li Qi saw the Mysterious Prime Emperor riding purple clouds and was told the dynasty's fortune would be prolonged."
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the Supreme Ultimate Palace reported that Academician Li Qi had seen the Mysterious Prime Emperor riding purple clouds and had been told the dynasty's fortune would endure."

sentences.zh: 唐初，詔敕皆書、門下官有文者為之。

translations.literal: In early Tang, all edicts and rescripts were drafted by literate officials of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In early Tang, edicts and rescripts were drafted by literate officials of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 乾封以後，始召文士元萬頃、范履冰等草諸文辭，常於北門候進止，時人謂之「北門學士」。

translations.literal: After the Qianfeng era, literary men such as Yuan Wanshu and Fan Lübing were first summoned to draft various compositions; they often waited at the north gate for orders to advance or halt, and people of the time called them the "Northern Gate Academicians."
translations.idiomatic: After the Qianfeng era, literary men such as Yuan Wanshu and Fan Lübing were summoned to draft court compositions; they often waited at the north gate for the emperor's word, and contemporaries called them the "Northern Gate Academicians."

sentences.zh: 中宗之世，上官昭容專其事。

translations.literal: In Zhongzong's time Shangguan Zhaorong monopolized the task.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhongzong, Shangguan Zhaorong monopolized the work.

sentences.zh: 上即位，始置翰林院，密邇禁廷，延文章之士，下至僧、道、書、畫、琴、棋、數術之工皆處之，謂之「待詔」。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne he first established the Hanlin Academy, close to the inner court, inviting men of letters—and extending down to monks, Daoists, calligraphers, painters, zither players, chess players, and masters of calculation and arts—all lodged there and called "Awaiting Imperial Command."
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong took the throne he established the Hanlin Academy beside the inner court, gathering men of letters and even monks, Daoists, calligraphers, painters, musicians, chess masters, and experts in calculation and the arts; they were called "awaiting imperial command."

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書張均及弟太常卿□皆翰林院供奉。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Zhang Jun and his younger brother, Grand Master of Ceremonies □, were both Hanlin Academy retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Zhang Jun and his younger brother, Grand Master of Ceremonies □, both served as Hanlin retainers.

sentences.zh: 上欲加安祿山同平章事，已令張□草制。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to add An Lushan as Associate Grand Councillor and had already ordered Zhang □ to draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to appoint An Lushan Associate Grand Councillor and had already ordered Zhang □ to draft the edict.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠諫曰：「祿山雖有軍功，目不知書，豈可為宰相！

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong remonstrated, saying, "Though Lushan has military merit, his eyes do not know writing—how can he be made chief minister!
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong remonstrated: "Lushan may have won battles, but he cannot even read—how can he be made chief minister!

sentences.zh: 制書若下，恐四夷輕唐。」

translations.literal: If the edict goes forth, I fear the four barbarians will look down on Tang."
translations.idiomatic: If that edict goes out, the four quarters will surely despise the Tang."

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，加祿山左僕射，賜一子三品、一子四品官。

translations.literal: On yisi Lushan was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; one son was granted third-rank office and one son fourth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi Lushan was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and one son was given third rank and another fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 丙午，上還宮。

translations.literal: On bingwu the emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 安祿山求兼領閒廄、群牧；

translations.literal: An Lushan requested to hold concurrently the Imperial Stud and the herd offices.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan asked to take charge of the Imperial Stud and the herd offices as well.

sentences.zh: 庚申，以祿山為閒廄、隴右群牧等使。

translations.literal: On gengshen Lushan was made commissioner of the Imperial Stud and Longyou herd offices, among others.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen he was appointed commissioner of the Imperial Stud and the Longyou herd offices, among other posts.

sentences.zh: 祿山又求兼總監；

translations.literal: Lushan again requested to hold the directorate concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan also asked to hold the directorate concurrently.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，兼知總監事。

translations.literal: On renxu he was made to know the affairs of the directorate concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu he was given concurrent charge of the directorate.

sentences.zh: 祿山奏以御史中丞吉溫為武部侍郎，充閒廄逼使，楊國忠由是惡溫。

translations.literal: Lushan memorialized that Censor-in-Chief Ji Wen be made Vice Minister of War and serve as vice commissioner of the Imperial Stud; Yang Guozhong therefore came to hate Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan memorialized that Censor-in-Chief Ji Wen be made Vice Minister of War and deputy commissioner of the Imperial Stud; from this Yang Guozhong came to hate Wen.

sentences.zh: 祿山密遣親信選健馬堪戰者數千匹，別飼之。

translations.literal: Lushan secretly sent trusted agents to select several thousand sturdy horses fit for battle and fed them separately.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan secretly sent trusted men to pick out several thousand sturdy war horses and had them fed apart from the rest.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬申，上朝獻太清宮，上聖祖尊號曰大聖祖高上大道金闕玄元大皇太帝。

translations.literal: In the second month, on renshen, the emperor paid court at the Supreme Ultimate Palace and elevated the sage ancestor's honorific title to Great Sage Ancestor, Exalted Supreme Great Way, Golden Portal, Mysterious Prime Great August Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on renshen, the emperor attended court at the Supreme Ultimate Palace and raised his sage ancestor's honorific to Great Sage Ancestor, Exalted Supreme Great Way, Golden Portal, Mysterious Prime Great August Emperor.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，享太廟，上高祖謚曰神堯大聖光孝皇帝，太宗謚曰文武大聖大廣孝皇帝，高宗謚曰天皇大聖大弘孝皇帝，中宗謚曰孝和大聖大昭孝皇帝，睿宗謚曰玄真大聖大興孝皇帝，以漢家諸帝皆謚孝故也。

translations.literal: On guiyou he offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, elevating Gaozu's posthumous title to Divine Yao Great Sage Luminous Filial Emperor, Taizong's to Civil and Martial Great Sage Great Expansive Filial Emperor, Gaozong's to Heavenly Sovereign Great Sage Great Magnificent Filial Emperor, Zhongzong's to Filial Harmony Great Sage Great Illustrious Filial Emperor, and Ruizong's to Mysterious Perfection Great Sage Great Flourishing Filial Emperor—because Han emperors all bore the posthumous element "Filial."
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou he sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, raising Gaozu's posthumous name to Divine Yao Great Sage Luminous Filial Emperor, Taizong's to Civil and Martial Great Sage Great Expansive Filial Emperor, Gaozong's to Heavenly Sovereign Great Sage Great Magnificent Filial Emperor, Zhongzong's to Filial Harmony Great Sage Great Illustrious Filial Emperor, and Ruizong's to Mysterious Perfection Great Sage Great Flourishing Filial Emperor—for Han emperors had all taken "Filial" in their posthumous names.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，群臣上尊號曰開元天地大寶聖文神武證道孝德皇帝。

translations.literal: On jiaxu the officials presented the honorific title Kaiyuan Heaven and Earth Great Treasure Sage Culture Divine Martial Proving the Way Filial Virtue Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu the officials presented the honorific Kaiyuan Heaven and Earth Great Treasure Sage Culture Divine Martial Proving the Way Filial Virtue Emperor.

sentences.zh: 赦天下。

translations.literal: He proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，楊國忠進位司空；

translations.literal: On dingchou Yang Guozhong was advanced to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Yang Guozhong was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 甲申，臨軒冊命。

translations.literal: On jiashen the investiture was performed before the throne hall.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen the investiture ceremony was held at the throne hall.

sentences.zh: 己丑，安祿山奏：「臣所部將士討奚、契丹、九姓、同羅等，勳效甚多，乞不拘常格，超資加賞，仍好寫告身付臣軍授之。」

translations.literal: On jichou An Lushan memorialized: "The generals and soldiers under my command in campaigns against the Xi, Khitan, Nine Surnames, Tongluo, and others have achieved much merit; I beg that they not be bound by ordinary rules but be rewarded beyond their rank, and that blank commission documents be prepared and handed to my army for me to confer."
translations.idiomatic: On jichou An Lushan memorialized: "My officers and men who fought the Xi, Khitan, Nine Surnames, Tongluo, and others have won great merit; I ask that they be rewarded beyond the usual rules and that blank commissions be sent to my army for me to fill and award."

sentences.zh: 於是除將軍者五百餘人，中郎將者二千餘人。

translations.literal: Thereupon more than five hundred were appointed generals and more than two thousand made commandants of the palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: More than five hundred were made generals and more than two thousand commandants of the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 祿山欲反，故先以此收眾心也。

translations.literal: Lushan intended to rebel and therefore first used this to win men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan was already planning rebellion and used this first to win the troops' loyalty.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁酉朔，祿山辭歸范陽。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the dingyou new moon, Lushan took leave and returned to Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the dingyou new moon, Lushan took his leave and returned to Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 上解御衣以賜之，祿山受之驚喜。

translations.literal: The emperor removed his imperial robe to bestow it; Lushan received it with startled joy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took off his own robe and gave it to him; Lushan accepted it in startled delight.

sentences.zh: 恐楊國忠奏留之，疾驅出關。

translations.literal: Fearing Yang Guozhong would memorialize to detain him, he whipped his horses and dashed out through the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Yang Guozhong would ask the court to keep him, he whipped his horses and raced out through the pass.

sentences.zh: 乘船沿河而下，令船夫執繩板立於岸側，十五里一更，晝夜兼行，日數百里，過郡縣不下船。

translations.literal: He took boat down the river, ordering boatmen to hold tow-ropes and boards standing on the banks; every fifteen li they changed teams, traveling day and night together, covering several hundred li a day, passing through prefectures and counties without leaving the boat.
translations.idiomatic: He went by boat downriver, with tow-teams stationed on the banks every fifteen li; traveling day and night without pause he covered several hundred li a day and never left the boat even when passing through prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 自是有言祿山反者，上皆縛送之。

translations.literal: From this time, whoever said Lushan would rebel—the emperor had them bound and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, anyone who said Lushan would rebel was bound and handed over to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 由是人皆知其將反，無敢言者。

translations.literal: Thus everyone knew he would rebel, yet none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone knew he would rebel, yet no one dared say so.

sentences.zh: 祿山之發長安也，上令高力士餞之長樂坡，及還，上問：「祿山慰意乎？」

translations.literal: When Lushan was leaving Chang'an, the emperor ordered Gao Lishi to give him a farewell at Changle Slope; when Lishi returned, the emperor asked, "Is Lushan content?"
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan left Chang'an, the emperor sent Gao Lishi to see him off at Changle Slope; on his return the emperor asked, "Did Lushan seem content?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「觀其意怏怏，必知欲命為相而中止故也。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Judging by his sullen manner, he must know he was to be appointed chief minister and that it was stopped."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "He looked sullen—he must know he was to be made chief minister and that the appointment was stopped."

sentences.zh: 上以告國忠，曰：「此議他人不知，必張□兄弟告之也。」

translations.literal: The emperor told Guozhong and said, "Others did not know of this plan—it must have been the Zhang □ brothers who told him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Guozhong, "No one else knew of this—it must have been the Zhang □ brothers who told him."

sentences.zh: 上怒，貶張均為建安太守，□為盧溪司馬，□弟給事中埱為宜春司馬。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and demoted Zhang Jun to prefect of Jian'an, □ to Lixi Sima, and □'s younger brother, Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang, to Yichun Sima.
translations.idiomatic: In anger the emperor demoted Zhang Jun to prefect of Jian'an, □ to Lixi Sima, and □'s younger brother Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang to Yichun Sima.

sentences.zh: 哥舒翰亦為其部將論功，敕以隴右十將、特進、火拔州都督、燕山郡王火拔歸仁為驃騎大將軍，河源軍使王思禮加特進，臨洮太守成如璆、討擊副使范陽魯炅、皋蘭府都督渾惟明並加雲麾將軍，隴右討擊副使郭英乂為左羽林將軍。

translations.literal: Geshu Han also had merit argued for his subordinate generals; an edict made Longyou's ten generals, including Special Advancement Holder, Huoba Prefecture Protector, and Yanshan Commandery King Huoba Guiren, General of Agile Cavalry; Heyuan Army commissioner Wang Silun was given Special Advancement; Lintao prefect Cheng Ruqiu, campaign vice-commissioner Fanyang Lu Jiong, and Gaolan Protectorate Protector Hun Weiming were all promoted to Cloud-Banner Generals; Longyou campaign vice-commissioner Guo Yingyi was made Left General of the Forest of Feathers.
translations.idiomatic: Geshu Han too had his subordinates' merits argued; by edict Huoba Guiren of the ten Longyou generals—Special Advancement Holder, Huoba prefect, and King of Yanshan—was made General of Agile Cavalry; Heyuan army commissioner Wang Silun received Special Advancement; Lintao prefect Cheng Ruqiu, campaign vice-commissioner Lu Jiong of Fanyang, and Gaolan protectorate protector Hun Weiming were all made Cloud-Banner Generals; and Longyou campaign vice-commissioner Guo Yingyi was made Left General of the Forest of Feathers.

sentences.zh: 英乂，知運之子也。

translations.literal: Yingyi was the son of Zhiyun.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyi was the son of Guo Zhiyun.

sentences.zh: 翰又奏嚴挺之之子武為節度判官，河東呂諲為度支判官，前封丘尉高適為掌書記，安邑曲環為別將。

translations.literal: Han also memorialized that Yan Tingzhi's son Wu be made military commissioner aide, Hedong's Lü Shen revenue commissioner aide, former Fengqiu magistrate Gao Shi chief secretary, and Anyi Qu Huan deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: Han also memorialized that Yan Tingzhi's son Wu be made military commissioner aide, Lü Shen of Hedong revenue commissioner aide, former Fengqiu magistrate Gao Shi chief secretary, and Qu Huan of Anyi deputy general.

sentences.zh: 程千里執阿布思，獻於闕下，斬之。

translations.literal: Cheng Qianli seized Ashina Busi, presented him at the palace gates, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Qianli captured Ashina Busi, presented him at court, and had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以千里為金吾大將軍，以封常清權北庭都護、伊西節度使。

translations.literal: On jiazi Qianli was made General of the Golden Guards; Feng Changqing was made acting Protector-General of Beiting and Yixi military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Qianli was made General of the Golden Guards, and Feng Changqing acting Protector-General of Beiting and Yixi military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸巳，安祿山奏擊奚破之，虜其王李日越。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on guisi, An Lushan memorialized that he had attacked and broken the Xi, capturing their king Li Riyue.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on guisi, An Lushan reported that he had defeated the Xi and captured their king Li Riyue.

sentences.zh: 六月，乙丑朔，日有食之，不盡如鉤。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the yichou new moon, there was a solar eclipse, not complete but like a hook.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the yichou new moon, there was a partial solar eclipse shaped like a hook.

sentences.zh: 侍御史、俞南留後李宓將兵七萬擊南詔。

translations.literal: Investigating censor and Yunnan rear-commissioner Li Mi led seventy thousand troops to attack Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor and Yunnan rear-commissioner Li Mi led seventy thousand men against Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 閣羅鳳誘之深入，至太和城，閉壁不戰。

translations.literal: Piluoge lured them deep in, and when they reached Taihe city he shut the walls and would not fight.
translations.idiomatic: Piluoge lured them deep inland; when they reached Taihe he shut the walls and refused battle.

sentences.zh: 宓糧盡，士卒罹瘴疫及饑死什七八，乃引還；

translations.literal: Mi's provisions were exhausted; seven or eight tenths of the soldiers died of miasma, plague, and hunger, and he then led them back.
translations.idiomatic: When Mi's supplies ran out, seven or eight soldiers in ten died of miasma, disease, and hunger, and he turned back.

sentences.zh: 蠻追擊之，宓被擒，全軍皆沒。

translations.literal: The barbarians pursued and struck; Mi was captured and the whole army perished.
translations.idiomatic: The tribesmen pursued them; Mi was captured and the entire army was lost.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠隱其敗，更以捷聞，益發中國兵討之，前後死者幾二十萬人，無敢言者。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong concealed the defeat and instead reported victory; he sent more Chinese troops to campaign, and those who died before and after approached two hundred thousand, yet none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong hid the defeat and reported a victory instead; he sent more central troops to campaign, and nearly two hundred thousand died in all—yet no one dared speak of it.

sentences.zh: 上嘗謂高力士曰：「朕今老矣，朝事付之宰相，邊事付之諸將，夫復何憂！」

translations.literal: The emperor once said to Gao Lishi, "I am old now; court affairs I entrust to the chief ministers, frontier affairs to the generals—what more is there to worry about!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told Gao Lishi, "I am old now; I leave court affairs to the chief ministers and frontier affairs to the generals—what is left to worry about!"

sentences.zh: 力士對曰：「臣聞雲南數喪師，又邊將擁兵太盛，陛下將何以制之！

translations.literal: Lishi replied, "Your servant has heard that Yunnan has repeatedly lost armies, and moreover the frontier generals hold troops in excessive strength—how will Your Majesty control them!
translations.idiomatic: Lishi replied, "I hear Yunnan has lost army after army, and the frontier generals' armies are too strong—how will Your Majesty control them?

sentences.zh: 臣恐一旦禍發，不可復救，何謂無憂也！」

translations.literal: Your servant fears that once disaster breaks out it cannot be remedied—how can you say there is nothing to worry about!"
translations.idiomatic: I fear that once disaster strikes it cannot be undone—how can you say there is nothing to worry about!"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿勿言，朕徐思之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Do not speak further; I shall think on it in due time."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Say no more; I will think on it in time."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸丑，哥舒翰奏，於所開九曲之地置洮陽、澆河二郡及神策軍，以臨洮太守成如璆兼洮陽太守，充神策軍使。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on guichou, Geshu Han memorialized that in the land of the opened Nine Bends he established Taoyang and Jiaohe commanderies and the Divine Strategy Army, with Lintao prefect Cheng Ruqiu concurrently Taoyang prefect and serving as Divine Strategy Army commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on guichou, Geshu Han memorialized that in the Nine Bends territory he had set up Taoyang and Jiaohe commanderies and the Divine Strategy Army, with Lintao prefect Cheng Ruqiu also Taoyang prefect and commissioner of that army.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠忌陳希烈，希烈累表辭位；

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong resented Chen Xilie; Xilie repeatedly memorialized to resign his post.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong resented Chen Xilie, who repeatedly asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 上欲以武部侍郎吉溫代之，國忠以溫附安祿山，奏言不可；

translations.literal: The emperor wished to replace him with Vice Minister of War Ji Wen; Guozhong, because Wen was attached to An Lushan, memorialized that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to replace him with Vice Minister of War Ji Wen, but Guozhong, because Wen was close to An Lushan, memorialized against it.

sentences.zh: 以文部侍郎韋見素和雅易制，薦之。

translations.literal: He recommended Vice Minister of Rites Wei Jiansu as mild, refined, and easy to control.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Vice Minister of Rites Wei Jiansu as mild, refined, and easy to control.

sentences.zh: 八月，丙戌，以希烈為太子太師，罷政事；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on bingxu, Xilie was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and removed from administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on bingxu, Xilie was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 以見素為武部尚書、同平章事。

translations.literal: Jiansu was made Minister of War and Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Jiansu was made Minister of War and Associate Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 自去歲水旱相繼，關中大饑。

translations.literal: From last year flood and drought followed one another, and Guanzhong suffered great famine.
translations.idiomatic: Since the previous year floods and droughts had followed one another, and Guanzhong was in severe famine.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠惡京兆尹李峴不附己，以災沴歸咎於峴，九月，貶長沙太守。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong hated Metropolitan Magistrate Li Xian for not attaching himself to him; he blamed the calamities on Xian, and in the ninth month demoted him to prefect of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong hated Metropolitan Magistrate Li Xian for refusing to follow him; he blamed the disasters on Xian and in the ninth month demoted him to prefect of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 峴，禕之子也。

translations.literal: Xian was the son of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was the son of Li Yi.

sentences.zh: 上憂雨傷稼，國忠取禾之善者獻之，曰：「雨雖多，不害稼也。」

translations.literal: The emperor worried that rain was harming the crops; Guozhong took good grain and presented it, saying, "Though the rain is heavy, it does not harm the crops."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor worried the rains were ruining the harvest; Guozhong brought him fine grain and said, "Heavy as the rain is, it has not harmed the crops."

sentences.zh: 上以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed him.

sentences.zh: 扶風太守房琯言所部水災，國忠使御史推之。

translations.literal: Fufeng prefect Fang Guan reported flooding in his jurisdiction; Guozhong sent censors to investigate him.
translations.idiomatic: Fufeng prefect Fang Guan reported flooding in his district; Guozhong sent censors to investigate him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，天下無敢言災者。

translations.literal: That year, throughout the realm none dared speak of disaster.
translations.idiomatic: That year no one in the realm dared report disasters.

sentences.zh: 高力士侍側，上曰：「淫雨不已，卿可盡言。」

translations.literal: Gao Lishi attended at his side; the emperor said, "The excessive rain does not cease—you may speak fully."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lishi was in attendance; the emperor said, "The rains will not stop—you may speak freely."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「自陛下以權假宰相，賞罰無章，陰陽失度，臣何敢言！」

translations.literal: He replied, "Since Your Majesty has lent authority to the chief minister, rewards and punishments lack rule and yin and yang have lost their measure—how dare your servant speak!"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Since Your Majesty has given the chief minister such power, rewards and punishments have no rule and heaven and earth are out of balance—how dare I speak!"

sentences.zh: 上默然。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，乙酉，上幸華清宮。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on yiyou, the emperor visited Huaqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on yiyou, the emperor went to Huaqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 十一月，己未，置內侍監二員，正三品。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jiwei, two posts of Director of Palace Attendants were established, of the third rank proper.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jiwei, two Directors of Palace Attendants of the third rank were established.

sentences.zh: 河東太守兼本道採訪使韋陟，斌之兄也，文雅有盛名，楊國忠恐其入相，使人告陟贓污事，下御史按問。

translations.literal: Hedong prefect and circuit investigating commissioner Wei Zhi, elder brother of Bin, was refined and literary and enjoyed great fame; Yang Guozhong feared he would enter the chief ministership and had someone report Zhi's corruption; censors were sent to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong prefect and circuit investigating commissioner Wei Zhi—elder brother of Wei Bin—was refined and famous; Yang Guozhong, fearing he would become chief minister, had someone accuse him of corruption, and censors were sent to investigate.

sentences.zh: 陟賂中丞吉溫，使求救於安祿山，復為國忠所發。

translations.literal: Zhi bribed Chief Censor Ji Wen to seek rescue from An Lushan, but this too was exposed by Guozhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi bribed Chief Censor Ji Wen to ask An Lushan for help, but Guozhong exposed that as well.

sentences.zh: 閏月，壬寅，貶陟桂嶺尉，溫澧陽長史。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on renyin, Zhi was demoted to Guiling commandant and Wen to Liyang chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on renyin, Zhi was demoted to Guiling commandant and Wen to Liyang chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 安祿山為溫訟冤，且言國忠讒疾。

translations.literal: An Lushan pleaded Wen's injustice and also said Guozhong slandered and resented him.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan pleaded Wen's case and accused Guozhong of slander and malice.

sentences.zh: 上兩無所問。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned neither side.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned neither side.

sentences.zh: 戊午，上還宮。

translations.literal: On wuwu the emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 是歲，戶部奏天下郡三百二十一，縣千五百三十八，鄉萬六千八百二十九，戶九百六萬九千一百五十四，口五千二百八十八萬四百八十八。

translations.literal: That year the Ministry of Revenue reported throughout the realm 321 commanderies, 1,538 counties, 16,829 townships, 9,069,154 households, and 52,880,488 persons.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Ministry of Revenue reported 321 commanderies, 1,538 counties, 16,829 townships, 9,069,154 households, and a population of 52,880,488.

sentences.zh: 玄宗至道大聖大明孝皇帝下之下天寶十四年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong of Tang, Latter Part of the Lower Scroll, Tianbao year 14 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong of Tang, Latter Part of the Lower Scroll, Tianbao year 14 (

sentences.zh: 乙未，公元七五五年）

translations.literal: yiwei, AD 755)
translations.idiomatic: yiwei, AD 755)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，蘇毘王子悉諾邏去吐蕃來降。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the Suibi prince Xinuoluo left Tibet and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the Suibi prince Xinuoluo left Tibet and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛亥，安祿山使副將何千年入奏，請以蕃將三十二人代漢將，上命立進畫，給告身。

translations.literal: In the second month, on xinhai, An Lushan sent his deputy general He Qiannian to memorialize, requesting that thirty-two barbarian generals replace Han generals; the emperor ordered immediate advancement and portraits and commission documents to be issued.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinhai, An Lushan sent his deputy He Qiannian to court to ask that thirty-two non-Han generals replace Han commanders; the emperor ordered their immediate promotion, portraits, and commissions issued.

sentences.zh: 韋見素謂楊國忠曰：「祿山久有異志，今又有此請，其反明矣。

translations.literal: Wei Jiansu said to Yang Guozhong, "Lushan has long harbored divergent intent; now with this request as well, his rebellion is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jiansu told Yang Guozhong, "Lushan has long had rebellious designs; with this request his intent is plain.

sentences.zh: 明日見素當極言；

translations.literal: Tomorrow Jiansu will speak to the utmost;
translations.idiomatic: Tomorrow I will speak out fully;

sentences.zh: 上未允，公其繼之。」

translations.literal: if the emperor does not assent, you must follow up."
translations.idiomatic: if the emperor does not agree, you must follow with your support."

sentences.zh: 國忠許諾。

translations.literal: Guozhong promised.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong agreed.

sentences.zh: 壬子，國忠、見素入見，上迎謂曰：「卿等有疑祿山之意邪？」

translations.literal: On renzi Guozhong and Jiansu entered audience; the emperor met them and said, "Do you harbor doubts about Lushan?"
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Guozhong and Jiansu came to audience; the emperor met them and said, "Do you doubt Lushan?"

sentences.zh: 見素因極言祿山反已有跡，所請不可許，上不悅，國忠逡巡不敢言，上竟從祿山之請。

translations.literal: Jiansu then spoke to the utmost that Lushan's rebellion already had signs and the request could not be granted; the emperor was displeased, Guozhong hesitated and dared not speak, and the emperor ultimately followed Lushan's request.
translations.idiomatic: Jiansu then spoke out fully that Lushan's rebellion already showed clear signs and that the request must be refused; the emperor was displeased, Guozhong hung back and dared not speak, and in the end the emperor granted Lushan's request.

sentences.zh: 他日，國忠、見素言於上曰：「臣有策可坐消祿山之謀。

translations.literal: Another day Guozhong and Jiansu said to the emperor, "Your servant has a plan that can sit and dissolve Lushan's plot.
translations.idiomatic: On another day Guozhong and Jiansu told the emperor, "We have a plan that can quietly undo Lushan's scheme.

sentences.zh: 今若除祿山平章事，召詣闕，以賈循為范陽節度使，呂知誨為平盧節度使，楊光翽為河東節度使，則勢自分矣。」

translations.literal: If now Lushan is removed as Grand Councillor, summoned to court, Jia Xun made Fanyang military commissioner, Lü Zhihui made Pinglu military commissioner, and Yang Guangbi made Hedong military commissioner, then his power will divide of itself."
translations.idiomatic: If Lushan is removed as Grand Councillor and summoned to court, with Jia Xun made Fanyang military commissioner, Lü Zhihui Pinglu military commissioner, and Yang Guangbi Hedong military commissioner, his power will split of itself."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 已草制，上留不發，更遣中使輔璆琳以珍果賜祿山，潛察其變。

translations.literal: The edict was already drafted, but the emperor kept it from being issued and instead sent palace envoy Fu Yuolin with rare fruits to bestow on Lushan, secretly to observe his changes.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was drafted, but the emperor held it back and sent palace envoy Fu Yuolin with rare fruits to Lushan, secretly to watch for trouble.

sentences.zh: 璆琳受祿山厚賂，還，盛言祿山竭忠奉國，無有二心。

translations.literal: Yuolin received heavy bribes from Lushan; on returning he spoke at length that Lushan exhausted his loyalty in serving the state and had no second heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yuolin took heavy bribes from Lushan; on his return he insisted that Lushan was utterly loyal and had no second thoughts.

sentences.zh: 上謂國忠等曰：「祿山，朕推心待之，必無異志。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Guozhong and the others, "Lushan—I treat him with an open heart and he surely has no divergent intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Guozhong and the others, "I have given Lushan my full trust; he cannot have rebellious intent.

sentences.zh: 東北二虜，藉其鎮遏。

translations.literal: The two barbarians of the northeast rely on him to hold them in check.
translations.idiomatic: The two northeastern tribes depend on him to keep them in check.

sentences.zh: 朕自保之，卿等勿憂也！」

translations.literal: I myself will keep him secure—you need not worry!"
translations.idiomatic: I will keep him in hand myself—you need not worry!"

sentences.zh: 事遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 循，華原人也，時為節度副使。

translations.literal: Xun was a man of Huayuan and at the time was military vice-commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was from Huayuan and was then military vice-commissioner.

sentences.zh: 隴右、河西節度使哥舒翰入朝，道得風疾，遂留京師，家居不出。

translations.literal: Longyou and Hexi military commissioner Geshu Han came to court, but on the road contracted wind illness and therefore remained in the capital, staying at home and not going out.
translations.idiomatic: Longyou and Hexi military commissioner Geshu Han came to court but fell ill with paralysis on the road; he remained in the capital and stayed home, never going out.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛巳，命給事中裴士淹宣慰河北。

translations.literal: In the third month, on xinsi, Attendant-in-Ordinary Pei Shiyan was ordered to comfort Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on xinsi, Attendant-in-Ordinary Pei Shiyan was sent to comfort Hebei.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，安祿山奏破奚、契丹。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, An Lushan memorialized that he had broken the Xi and Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, An Lushan reported victories over the Xi and Khitan.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以蘇毘王子悉諾邏為懷義王，賜姓名李忠信。

translations.literal: On guisi the Suibi prince Xinuoluo was made Prince of Huaiyi and granted the surname and personal name Li Zhongxin.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the Suibi prince Xinuoluo was made Prince of Huaiyi and given the name Li Zhongxin.

sentences.zh: 安祿山歸至范陽，朝廷每遣使者至，皆稱疾不出迎，盛陳武備，然後見之。

translations.literal: An Lushan returned to Fanyang; whenever the court sent envoys, he claimed illness and would not come out to receive them, arraying arms in great display before then seeing them.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan returned to Fanyang, he claimed illness whenever court envoys arrived, paraded his forces, and only then received them.

sentences.zh: 裴士淹至范陽，二十餘日乃得見，無復人臣禮。

translations.literal: Pei Shiyan reached Fanyang and only after more than twenty days obtained an audience, with no further observance of a subject's rites.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shiyan reached Fanyang and waited more than twenty days for an audience, and Lushan no longer observed the rites of a subject.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠日夜求祿山反狀，使京兆尹圍其第，捕祿山客李超等，送御史台獄，潛殺之。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong day and night sought evidence of Lushan's rebellion, had the metropolitan magistrate surround his residence, arrested Lushan's clients Li Chao and others, sent them to the censorate prison, and secretly killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong searched day and night for proof of rebellion, had the metropolitan magistrate surround Lushan's residence, arrested clients such as Li Chao, sent them to the censorate prison, and secretly killed them.

sentences.zh: 祿山子慶宗尚宗女榮義郡主，供奉在京師，密報祿山，祿山愈懼。

translations.literal: Lushan's son Qingzong had married the emperor's daughter Princess Rongyi and served at court in the capital; he secretly reported to Lushan, and Lushan grew all the more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan's son Qingzong, who had married Princess Rongyi and served at court, secretly warned his father, and Lushan grew more afraid.

sentences.zh: 六月，上以其子成婚，於詔召祿山觀禮，祿山辭疾不至。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, because his son was marrying, the emperor issued an edict summoning Lushan to observe the ceremony; Lushan pleaded illness and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the emperor summoned Lushan to attend his son's wedding, but Lushan pleaded illness and did not come.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，祿山表獻馬三千匹，每匹執控夫二人，遣蕃將二十二人部送。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Lushan memorialized presenting three thousand horses, each with two grooms holding the reins, and sent twenty-two barbarian generals to escort them.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Lushan offered three thousand horses, each with two handlers, escorted by twenty-two non-Han generals.

sentences.zh: 河南尹達奚珣疑有變，奏請「諭祿山以進車馬宜俟至冬，官自給夫，無煩本軍。」

translations.literal: Henan metropolitan magistrate Daxi Xun suspected trouble and memorialized requesting "to instruct Lushan that presenting chariots and horses should wait until winter, with the government supplying laborers itself, without troubling his own army."
translations.idiomatic: Henan metropolitan magistrate Daxi Xun suspected a plot and memorialized that Lushan should be told, "Wait until winter to present the horses, with the government supplying the handlers so his army need not come."

sentences.zh: 於是上稍寤，始有疑祿山之意。

translations.literal: From this the emperor slightly awakened and first harbored doubts about Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor began to wake to the danger and first doubted Lushan.

sentences.zh: 會輔璆琳受賂事亦洩，上托以他事撲殺之。

translations.literal: When Fu Yuolin's taking bribes also leaked out, the emperor had him beaten to death on a pretext.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Yuolin's bribes also came to light, the emperor had him beaten to death on another charge.

sentences.zh: 上遣中使馮神威繼手詔諭祿山，如珣策；

translations.literal: The emperor sent palace envoy Feng Shenwei with a handwritten edict to instruct Lushan according to Xun's plan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent palace envoy Feng Shenwei with a handwritten edict to Lushan along the lines Xun had proposed.

sentences.zh: 且曰：朕新為卿作一湯，十月於華清宮待卿。」

translations.literal: and further said: I have newly prepared a bath for you; in the tenth month I shall await you at Huaqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He also added, "I have just had a hot spring prepared for you; in the tenth month I shall await you at Huaqing Palace."

sentences.zh: 神威至范陽宣旨，祿山踞床微起，亦不拜，曰：「聖人安隱。」

translations.literal: Shenwei reached Fanyang and proclaimed the decree; Lushan sat on his bed and rose slightly, yet did not bow, saying, "The Sage is secure and at ease."
translations.idiomatic: When Shenwei reached Fanyang and announced the decree, Lushan sat on his bed and barely rose, did not bow, and said only, "The Sage is well."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「馬不獻亦可，十月灼然詣京師。」

translations.literal: He also said, "The horses need not be presented; in the tenth month I shall clearly come to the capital."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "The horses need not be sent; in the tenth month I shall certainly come to the capital."

sentences.zh: 即令左右引神威置館舍，不復見；

translations.literal: He at once ordered attendants to lead Shenwei to lodge and did not see him again.
translations.idiomatic: He had attendants lodge Shenwei and did not see him again.

sentences.zh: 數日，遣還，亦無表。

translations.literal: After several days he sent him back, and there was no memorial either.
translations.idiomatic: After several days he sent him back without a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 神威還，見上，泣曰：「臣幾不得見大家！」

translations.literal: Shenwei returned and saw the emperor, weeping and saying, "Your servant nearly did not return to see His Majesty!"
translations.idiomatic: On his return Shenwei saw the emperor and wept, "I nearly never came back to see Your Majesty!"

sentences.zh: 八月，辛卯，免今載百姓租庸。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on xinmao, this year's land tax and corvée labor service for the people were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinmao, land tax and corvée for the year were remitted.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，庚寅，上幸華清宮。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on gengyin, the emperor visited Huaqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on gengyin, the emperor went to Huaqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 安祿山專制三道，陰蓄異志，殆將十年，以上待之厚，欲俟上晏駕然後作亂。

translations.literal: An Lushan monopolized the three circuits and secretly harbored divergent intent for nearly ten years; because the emperor treated him generously, he wished to wait until the emperor passed away before raising rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan had controlled three circuits and nursed rebellious designs for nearly ten years; because the emperor treated him so generously, he had meant to wait until Xuanzong died before rising.

sentences.zh: 會楊國忠與祿山不相悅，屢言祿山且反，上不聽；

translations.literal: It happened that Yang Guozhong and Lushan were not on good terms; he repeatedly said Lushan was about to rebel, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: But Yang Guozhong and Lushan were at odds; Guozhong kept saying Lushan would rebel soon, and the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 國忠數以事激之，欲其速反以取信於上。

translations.literal: Guozhong repeatedly provoked him with incidents, wishing him to rebel quickly so as to win the emperor's trust.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong kept provoking him, hoping to force an early rebellion and thereby win the emperor's trust.

sentences.zh: 祿山由是決意遽反，獨與孔目官、太僕丞嚴莊、掌書記、屯田員外郎高尚、將軍阿史那承慶密謀，自餘將佐皆莫之知，但怪其自八月以來，屢饗士卒，秣馬厲兵而已。

translations.literal: Lushan therefore resolved to rebel at once; he plotted secretly only with the registry officer, Grand Master of the Stud Yan Zhuang, chief secretary and Outer Office Director of Tuntian Gao Shang, and general Ashina Chengqing; the rest of the generals and aides knew nothing, but only wondered that since the eighth month he had repeatedly feasted the soldiers and fed horses and sharpened weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan therefore decided to rebel at once. He plotted secretly only with registry officer Yan Zhuang, chief secretary Gao Shang, and general Ashina Chengqing; the other officers knew nothing and only wondered why, since the eighth month, he had been feasting the troops and readying horses and arms.

sentences.zh: 會有奏事官自京師還，祿山詐為敕書，悉召諸將示之曰：「有密旨，令祿山將兵入朝討楊國忠，諸君宜即從軍。」

translations.literal: It happened that a memorializing official returned from the capital; Lushan forged an imperial edict, summoned all the generals, showed it to them, and said, "There is a secret decree ordering Lushan to lead troops to court to punish Yang Guozhong—you should all follow the army at once."
translations.idiomatic: When a court messenger returned from the capital, Lushan forged an imperial edict, summoned his generals, and said, "There is a secret order for me to lead troops to court to punish Yang Guozhong—you must all march at once."

sentences.zh: 眾愕然相顧，莫敢異言。

translations.literal: The crowd looked at one another in alarm and none dared speak otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: The men looked at one another in alarm and none dared object.

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲子，祿山發所部兵及同羅、奚、契丹、室韋凡十五萬眾，號二十萬，反於范陽。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jiazi, Lushan mobilized his own troops together with Tongluo, Xi, Khitan, and Shiwei—altogether one hundred fifty thousand men, proclaimed as two hundred thousand—and rebelled at Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jiazi, Lushan mobilized his own troops with Tongluo, Xi, Khitan, and Shiwei allies—one hundred fifty thousand men in all, called two hundred thousand—and rebelled at Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 命范陽節度副使賈循守范陽，平盧節度副使呂知誨守平盧，別將高秀巖守大同；

translations.literal: He ordered Fanyang military vice-commissioner Jia Xun to hold Fanyang, Pinglu military vice-commissioner Lü Zhihui to hold Pinglu, and detached general Gao Xiuyan to hold Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He left Fanyang vice-commissioner Jia Xun to hold Fanyang, Pinglu vice-commissioner Lü Zhihui to hold Pinglu, and detached general Gao Xiuyan to hold Datong.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆引兵夜發。

translations.literal: All the generals led their troops away by night.
translations.idiomatic: All the generals marched out by night.

sentences.zh: 詰朝，祿山出薊城南，大閱誓眾，以討楊國忠為名，榜軍中曰：「有異議扇動軍人者，斬及三族！」

translations.literal: At dawn Lushan went out south of Ji city, held a great review and swore the host, taking punishing Yang Guozhong as his name, and posted in the army: "Whoever raises dissent and stirs the soldiers—execution extending to three clans!"
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Lushan marched out south of Ji, reviewed the army, and swore them to punish Yang Guozhong; he posted a notice: "Anyone who stirs dissent among the troops will be executed, together with three generations of his family."

sentences.zh: 於是引兵而南。

translations.literal: He then led the army south.
translations.idiomatic: Then he led the army south.

sentences.zh: 祿山乘鐵輿，步騎精銳，煙塵千里，鼓噪震地。

translations.literal: Lushan rode in an iron carriage; infantry and cavalry were elite; dust and smoke stretched a thousand li; drums and shouts shook the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan rode in an iron carriage at the head of crack infantry and cavalry; dust filled the horizon for a thousand li and the drums shook the earth.

sentences.zh: 時海內久承平，百姓累世不識兵革，猝聞范陽兵起，遠近震駭。

translations.literal: The realm within the seas had long enjoyed peace; the people for generations had not known arms; suddenly hearing that Fanyang's army had risen, near and far were shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: The empire had been at peace so long that generations had never known war; when word came that the army of Fanyang had risen, terror spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 河北皆祿山統內，所過州縣，望風瓦解。

translations.literal: Hebei was all within Lushan's jurisdiction; the prefectures and counties he passed collapsed at the wind's report.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei lay entirely within Lushan's command; the prefectures and counties he passed melted away without a fight.

sentences.zh: 守令或開門出迎，或棄城竄匿，或為所擒戮，無敢拒之者。

translations.literal: Magistrates and prefects either opened the gates to welcome him, abandoned the cities and fled into hiding, or were seized and killed by him—none dared resist.
translations.idiomatic: Some magistrates opened their gates to welcome him, others abandoned their cities and fled, and others were captured and killed—none dared resist.

sentences.zh: 祿山先遣將軍何千年、高邈將奚騎二十，聲言獻射生手，乘驛詣太原。

translations.literal: Lushan first sent generals He Qiannian and Gao Miao with twenty Xi horsemen, claiming to present archers of the hunt, riding post-horses to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan first sent generals He Qiannian and Gao Miao with twenty Xi horsemen, claiming to present hunting archers, and they rode post relays to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，北京副留守楊光翽出迎，因劫之以去。

translations.literal: On yichou Northern Capital vice-commissioner Yang Guangbi came out to welcome them and was seized and taken away.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Northern Capital vice-commissioner Yang Guangbi came out to welcome them and was seized and carried off.

sentences.zh: 太原具言其狀。

translations.literal: Taiyuan fully reported the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan reported the whole affair in detail.

sentences.zh: 東受降城亦奏祿山反。

translations.literal: Eastern Surrender-Receiving City also memorialized that Lushan had rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Surrender-Receiving City also reported that Lushan had rebelled.

sentences.zh: 上猶以為惡祿山者詐為之，未之信也。

translations.literal: The emperor still thought those who hated Lushan had fabricated it and did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still thought Lushan's enemies had fabricated the reports and would not believe them.

sentences.zh: 庚午，上聞祿山定反，乃召宰相謀之。

translations.literal: On gengwu the emperor heard that Lushan had certainly rebelled and summoned the chief ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu the emperor learned that Lushan had indeed rebelled and summoned the chief ministers to plan.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠揚揚有得色，曰：「今反者獨祿山耳，將士皆不欲也。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong looked pleased with himself and said, "Now the rebel is Lushan alone; the generals and soldiers all do not wish it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong looked triumphant and said, "Only Lushan has rebelled; his soldiers do not want this.

sentences.zh: 不過旬日，必傳首詣行在。」

translations.literal: In no more than ten days his head will surely be sent to the imperial camp."
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days his head will be sent to Your Majesty's camp."

sentences.zh: 上以為然，大臣相顧失色。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this correct; the great ministers looked at one another and changed color.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed him; the ministers looked at one another in dismay.

sentences.zh: 上遣特進畢思琛詣東京，金吾將軍程千里詣河東，各簡募數萬人，隨便團結以拒之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Special Advancement Holder Bi Sichen to the Eastern Capital and General of the Golden Guards Cheng Qianli to Hedong; each was to select and recruit tens of thousands of men and assemble them wherever convenient to resist.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Special Advancement Holder Bi Sichen to the Eastern Capital and General of the Golden Guards Cheng Qianli to Hedong, each to raise tens of thousands of men wherever they could to resist.

sentences.zh: 辛未，安西節度使封常清入朝，上問以討賊方略，常清大言曰：「今太平積久，故人望風憚賊。

translations.literal: On xinwei Anxi military commissioner Feng Changqing came to court; the emperor asked him for strategy against the rebels, and Changqing spoke boldly: "Now peace has accumulated long, so men fear the rebels at the wind's report.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Anxi military commissioner Feng Changqing came to court; asked for a plan against the rebels, he said boldly, "Peace has lasted so long that men flee at the mere report of the rebels.

sentences.zh: 然事有逆順，勢有奇變，臣請走馬詣東京，開府庫，募驍勇，挑馬棰渡河，計日取逆胡之首獻闕下！」

translations.literal: Yet affairs have compliance and defiance, and situations have strange turns; your servant requests to ride post-horses to the Eastern Capital, open the government storehouses, recruit the brave, spur horses and cross the river, and within counted days bring the rebel barbarian's head to present below the palace gates!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet fortune turns, and war has its surprises. Let me ride to the Eastern Capital, open the treasuries, raise brave men, cross the river at a gallop, and within days bring the rebel's head to court!"

sentences.zh: 上悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 壬申，以常清為范陽、平盧節度使。

translations.literal: On renshen Changqing was made Fanyang and Pinglu military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Changqing was made Fanyang and Pinglu military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 常清即日乘驛詣東京募兵，旬日，得六萬人；

translations.literal: Changqing that same day rode post to the Eastern Capital to recruit troops; within ten days he obtained sixty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing rode post that same day to the Eastern Capital to raise troops; within ten days he had sixty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 乃斷河陽橋，為守禦之備。

translations.literal: He then cut the Heyang Bridge and made preparations for defense.
translations.idiomatic: He then destroyed the Heyang Bridge and prepared to defend.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，祿山至博陵南，何千年等執楊光翽見祿山，責光翽以附楊國忠，斬之以徇。

translations.literal: On jiaxu Lushan reached south of Boling; He Qiannian and the others brought Yang Guangbi before Lushan, reproached Guangbi for attaching himself to Yang Guozhong, and beheaded him as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Lushan reached south of Boling; He Qiannian and the others brought Yang Guangbi before him, accused him of siding with Yang Guozhong, and beheaded him as a warning.

sentences.zh: 祿山使其將安忠志將精兵軍土門，忠志，奚人，祿山養為假子；

translations.literal: Lushan had his general An Zhongzhi lead elite troops to garrison Tumen; Zhongzhi was a Xi man whom Lushan had raised as a foster son.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan sent his general An Zhongzhi, a Xi man he had adopted, to garrison Tumen with elite troops.

sentences.zh: 又以張獻誠攝博陵太守，獻誠，守珪之子也。

translations.literal: He also had Zhang Xiancheng act as Boling prefect; Xiancheng was the son of Shougui.
translations.idiomatic: He also put Zhang Xiancheng, son of Zhang Shougui, in charge as Boling prefect.

sentences.zh: 祿山至蒿城，常山太守顏杲卿力不能拒，與長史袁履謙往迎之。

translations.literal: Lushan reached Hao city; Changshan prefect Yan Gaoqing, his strength insufficient to resist, went with Chief Administrator Yuan Lüqian to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan reached Hao city, Changshan prefect Yan Gaoqing, unable to resist, went with chief administrator Yuan Lüqian to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 祿山輒賜杲卿金紫，質其子弟，使仍守常山；

translations.literal: Lushan at once bestowed on Gaoqing gold and purple, took his sons and younger brothers as hostages, and had him continue to hold Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan at once gave Gaoqing gold and purple insignia, took his sons as hostages, and left him in charge of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 又使其將李欽湊將兵數千人守井陘口，以備西來諸軍。

translations.literal: He also had his general Li Qincou lead several thousand troops to hold Jingxing Pass against armies coming from the west.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent his general Li Qincou with several thousand men to hold Jingxing Pass against armies from the west.

sentences.zh: 杲卿歸，途中指其衣謂履謙曰：「何為著此？」

translations.literal: Gaoqing returned; on the road he pointed to his robes and said to Lüqian, "Why am I wearing these?"
translations.idiomatic: On the way back Gaoqing pointed to his robes and asked Lüqian, "Why am I wearing these?"

sentences.zh: 履謙悟其意，乃陰與杲卿謀起兵討祿山。

translations.literal: Lüqian understood his meaning and secretly plotted with Gaoqing to raise troops and punish Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: Lüqian understood, and the two secretly plotted to raise troops against Lushan.

sentences.zh: 杲卿，思魯之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Gaoqing was the great-great-grandson of Silu.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing was the great-great-grandson of Yan Silu.

sentences.zh: 丙子，上還宮。

translations.literal: On bingzi the emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 斬太僕卿安慶宗，賜榮義郡主自盡。

translations.literal: Grand Master of the Stud An Qingzong was beheaded, and Princess Rongyi was granted permission to take her own life.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of the Stud An Qingzong was beheaded, and Princess Rongyi was ordered to kill herself.

sentences.zh: 以朔方節度使安思順為戶部尚書，思順弟元貞為太僕卿。

translations.literal: Shuofang military commissioner An Sishun was made Minister of Revenue, and Sishun's younger brother Yuanzhen was made Grand Master of the Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Shuofang military commissioner An Sishun was made Minister of Revenue, and his brother Yuanzhen Grand Master of the Stud.

sentences.zh: 以朔方右廂兵馬使、九原太守郭子儀為朔方節度使，右羽林大將軍王承業為太原尹。

translations.literal: Shuofang Right Wing army and horse commissioner and Jiuyuan prefect Guo Ziyi was made Shuofang military commissioner, and Right General of the Forest of Feathers Wang Chengye was made metropolitan magistrate of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shuofang Right Wing army commissioner and Jiuyuan prefect Guo Ziyi was made Shuofang military commissioner, and Right General of the Forest of Feathers Wang Chengye metropolitan magistrate of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 置河南節度使，領陳留等十三郡，以衛尉卿猗氏張介然為之。

translations.literal: A Henan military commissioner was established, overseeing thirteen commanderies including Chenliu; Minister of the Guard Zhang Jieran of Yishi was made commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: A Henan military commissioner was created over thirteen commanderies including Chenliu, and Minister of the Guard Zhang Jieran of Yishi was appointed.

sentences.zh: 以程千里為潞州長史。

translations.literal: Cheng Qianli was made chief administrator of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Qianli was made chief administrator of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 諸郡當賊沖者，始置防禦使。

translations.literal: For commanderies in the rebels' path, defense commissioners were first established.
translations.idiomatic: Defense commissioners were first appointed in commanderies in the rebels' path.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以榮王琬為元帥，右金吾大將軍高仙芝副之，統諸軍東征。

translations.literal: On dingchou Prince Rong Wan was made commander-in-chief, with Right General of the Golden Guards Gao Xianzhi as his deputy, to command the armies on the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Prince Rong Wan was made commander-in-chief with Right General of the Golden Guards Gao Xianzhi as deputy to lead the eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 出內府錢帛，於京師募兵十一萬，號曰天武軍，旬日而集，皆市井子弟也。

translations.literal: Funds and silks from the inner treasury were issued to recruit one hundred ten thousand troops in the capital, called the Heavenly Martial Army; they assembled within ten days—all were sons of the market wards.
translations.idiomatic: Money and silk from the inner treasury were used to raise one hundred ten thousand men in the capital, called the Heavenly Martial Army; they assembled within ten days—all townsmen and market youths.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙戌，高仙芝將飛騎、擴騎及新募兵、邊兵在京師者合五萬人，發長安。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on bingxu, Gao Xianzhi led Flying Cavalry, Expanded Cavalry, newly recruited troops, and frontier soldiers in the capital—altogether fifty thousand men—and set out from Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on bingxu, Gao Xianzhi led fifty thousand Flying Cavalry, expanded cavalry, new recruits, and frontier troops stationed in the capital out of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 上遣宦者監門將軍邊令誠監其軍，屯於陝。

translations.literal: The emperor sent eunuch Gate Guard General Bian Lingcheng to supervise the army; they encamped at Shan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent eunuch Gate Guard General Bian Lingcheng to supervise the army, which encamped at Shan.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，安祿山自靈昌渡河，以絲亙約敗船及草木橫絕河流，一夕，冰合如浮梁，遂陷炅昌郡。

translations.literal: On dinghai An Lushan crossed the river from Lingchang, using silk to bind wrecked boats and trees laid across to block the stream; in one night the ice joined like a pontoon bridge, and he then took Lingchang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai An Lushan crossed the Yellow River from Lingchang, binding wrecked boats and brush into the current; overnight the ice formed a bridge, and he took Lingchang commandery.

sentences.zh: 祿山步騎散漫，人莫知其數，所過殘滅。

translations.literal: Lushan's infantry and cavalry spread out widely; none knew their number; wherever they passed they ravaged and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: His infantry and cavalry spread out in a vast host whose numbers no one could tell, ravaging everything in their path.

sentences.zh: 張介然至陳留才數日，祿山至，授兵乘城。

translations.literal: Zhang Jieran had reached Chenliu only a few days when Lushan arrived; he issued arms and manned the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jieran had been in Chenliu only a few days when Lushan arrived; he armed the men and manned the walls.

sentences.zh: 眾忷懼，不能守。

translations.literal: The crowd was alarmed and afraid and could not hold.
translations.idiomatic: The troops panicked and could not hold the city.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，太守郭納以城降。

translations.literal: On gengyin prefect Guo Na surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin prefect Guo Na surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 祿山入北郭，聞安慶宗死，慟哭曰：「我何罪，而殺我子！」

translations.literal: Lushan entered the northern suburb; hearing that An Qingzong was dead, he wailed and said, "What crime have I committed, that you kill my son!"
translations.idiomatic: Lushan entered the northern quarter; when he heard Qingzong was dead, he wailed, "What crime did I commit, that you killed my son!"

sentences.zh: 時陳留將士降者夾道近萬人，祿山皆殺之以快其忿；

translations.literal: At the time nearly ten thousand Chenliu officers and soldiers who had surrendered lined the road; Lushan killed them all to vent his rage.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly ten thousand Chenliu soldiers who had surrendered lined the road; Lushan killed them all to vent his rage.

sentences.zh: 斬張介然於軍門。

translations.literal: Zhang Jieran was beheaded at the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded Zhang Jieran before the army gate.

sentences.zh: 以其將李庭望為節度使，守陳留。

translations.literal: His general Li Tingwang was made military commissioner to hold Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: He made his general Li Tingwang military commissioner to hold Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，上下制欲親征，其朔方、河西、隴右兵留守城堡之外，皆赴行營，令節度使自將之，期二十日畢集。

translations.literal: On renchen the emperor issued a decree wishing to campaign in person; Shuofang, Hexi, and Longyou troops, apart from those left to guard fortresses and cities, were all to proceed to the field camp, with military commissioners leading them in person, to assemble completely within twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen the emperor announced he would campaign in person; Shuofang, Hexi, and Longyou troops, except garrisons left to hold the fortresses, were to march to the field camp under their commissioners' command, all to assemble within twenty days.

sentences.zh: 初，平原太守顏真卿知祿山且反，因霖雨，完城浚壕，料丁壯，實倉廩。

translations.literal: Earlier, Pingyuan prefect Yan Zhenqing knew Lushan was about to rebel; taking advantage of the rainy season, he repaired the walls, deepened the moats, mustered able-bodied men, and filled the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Pingyuan prefect Yan Zhenqing had known Lushan would rebel; during the rains he repaired the walls, deepened the moats, mustered able-bodied men, and filled the granaries.

sentences.zh: 祿山以其書生，易之。

translations.literal: Lushan, because he was a scholar, thought him easy.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan, thinking him only a scholar, underestimated him.

sentences.zh: 及祿山反，牒真卿以平原、博平兵七千人防河津，真卿遣平原司兵李平間道奏之。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled he sent a dispatch to Zhenqing with seven thousand troops of Pingyuan and Boping to guard the river crossings; Zhenqing sent Pingyuan registrar Li Ping by a hidden route to memorialize the court.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled he ordered Zhenqing to guard the river crossings with seven thousand men from Pingyuan and Boping; Zhenqing sent registrar Li Ping by a secret route to report to court.

sentences.zh: 上始聞祿山反，河北郡縣皆風靡，歎曰：「二十四郡，曾無一人義士邪！」

translations.literal: The emperor first heard that Lushan had rebelled; Hebei's commanderies and counties all collapsed at the wind's report, and he sighed, "Of twenty-four commanderies, was there not one man of righteousness!"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first heard of the rebellion, every Hebei commandery and county had collapsed, and he sighed, "Of twenty-four commanderies, was there not one loyal man!"

sentences.zh: 及平至，大喜，曰：「朕不識顏真卿作何狀，乃能如是！」

translations.literal: When Ping arrived he was greatly pleased and said, "I do not know what Yan Zhenqing looks like, yet he could do thus!"
translations.idiomatic: When Ping arrived he was overjoyed and said, "I do not even know what Yan Zhenqing looks like, yet he could do this!"

sentences.zh: 真卿使親客密懷購賊牒詣諸郡，由是諸郡多應者。

translations.literal: Zhenqing had trusted retainers secretly carry bounty proclamations for capturing rebels to the various commanderies, and thereafter many commanderies responded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing sent trusted agents secretly bearing reward notices for the capture of rebels to neighboring commanderies; many answered the call.

sentences.zh: 真卿，杲卿之從弟也。

translations.literal: Zhenqing was Gaoqing's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing was the younger cousin of Yan Gaoqing.

sentences.zh: 安祿山引兵向滎陽，太守崔無詖拒之；

translations.literal: An Lushan led troops toward Xingyang; prefect Cui Wubi resisted him.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan marched on Xingyang, but prefect Cui Wubi barred his way.

sentences.zh: 士卒乘城者，聞鼓角聲，自墜如雨。

translations.literal: Soldiers on the walls, hearing drum and horn sounds, fell of themselves like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers manning the walls, at the first sound of drums and horns, leapt from the battlements like rain.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，祿山陷滎陽，殺無詖，以其將武令珣守之。

translations.literal: On guisi, Lushan took Xingyang, killed Wubi, and had his general Wu Lingxun hold it.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Lushan captured Xingyang, killed Wubi, and left his general Wu Lingxun as garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 祿山聲勢益張，以其將田承嗣、安忠志、張孝忠為前鋒。

translations.literal: Lushan's momentum grew ever greater; he made his generals Tian Chengsi, An Zhongzhi, and Zhang Xiaozhong vanguard commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan's power swelled daily; he put Tian Chengsi, An Zhongzhi, and Zhang Xiaozhong at the head of his advance.

sentences.zh: 封常清所募兵皆白徒，未更訓練，屯武牢以拒賊；

translations.literal: The troops Feng Changqing had recruited were all raw levies, never yet trained, and camped at Wulao to resist the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Changqing's recruits were untrained civilians, whom he had stationed at Wulao to hold back the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊以鐵騎蹂之，官軍大敗。

translations.literal: The rebels trampled them with iron cavalry, and the imperial army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel iron cavalry rode them down, and the imperial troops broke in ruin.

sentences.zh: 常清收餘眾，戰於葵園，又敗；

translations.literal: Changqing gathered the survivors and fought at Kuai Garden, and was again defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing rallied the remnants and gave battle at Kuai Garden—again he was beaten.

sentences.zh: 戰上東門內，又敗。

translations.literal: He fought inside the Upper East Gate and was again defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again inside the Upper East Gate, and once more was routed.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，祿山陷東京，賊鼓噪自四門入，縱兵殺掠。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Lushan took the Eastern Capital; rebels with drums roaring entered through the four gates and let the troops kill and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou Lushan took the Eastern Capital; rebels stormed in through all four gates to the clamor of drums and went on a rampage of slaughter and looting.

sentences.zh: 常清戰於都亭驛，又敗；

translations.literal: Changqing fought at Duting Post and was again defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing fought at Duting Post and lost again.

sentences.zh: 退守宣仁門，又敗；

translations.literal: He fell back to hold the Xuanren Gate and was again defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He fell back to defend the Xuanren Gate—and was beaten yet again.

sentences.zh: 乃自苑西壞牆西走。

translations.literal: Then he broke through the ruined wall west of the park enclosure and fled west.
translations.idiomatic: At last he broke through the ruined wall west of the imperial park and fled westward.

sentences.zh: 河南尹達奚珣降於祿山。

translations.literal: Henan governor Dadao Xun surrendered to Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: Dadao Xun, governor of Henan, surrendered to Lushan.

sentences.zh: 留守李□謂御史中丞盧奕曰：「吾曹荷國重任，雖知力不敵，必死之！」

translations.literal: Acting governor Li □ said to Censor-in-Chief Lu Yi, "We bear the state's heavy charge; though we know our strength cannot match theirs, we must die for it!"
translations.idiomatic: Acting governor Li □ told Censor-in-Chief Lu Yi, "The empire has laid a grave burden on us; though we cannot match the enemy, we must die trying!"

sentences.zh: 奕許諾。

translations.literal: Yi agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Yi promised he would.

sentences.zh: □收殘兵數百，欲戰，皆棄□潰去；

translations.literal: □ gathered several hundred remnant troops and wished to fight, but all abandoned □ and fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: □ rallied a few hundred survivors and tried to make a stand, but the men bolted and scattered.

sentences.zh: □獨坐府中。

translations.literal: □ alone sat in the government office.
translations.idiomatic: □ sat alone in the administrative hall.

sentences.zh: 弈先遣妻子懷印間道走長安，朝服坐台中，左右皆散。

translations.literal: Yi first sent his wife and children with the seal by a secret route to Chang'an, then sat on the dais in court dress while his attendants all dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had sent his family ahead with the official seal by a hidden route to Chang'an; now, clad in court robes, he sat alone on the dais as his attendants melted away.

sentences.zh: 祿山屯於閒廄，使人執□、奕及採訪判官蔣清，皆殺之。

translations.literal: Lushan encamped at the spare stables and sent men to seize □, Yi, and Investigating Commissioner adjunct Jiang Qing; all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan camped in the spare imperial stables and had his men seize □, Yi, and investigating commissioner Jiang Qing—all were put to death.

sentences.zh: 奕罵祿山，數其罪，顧賊黨曰：「凡為人當知逆順。

translations.literal: Yi cursed Lushan and counted out his crimes, then turning to the rebel followers said, "Every man should know loyalty and treason.
translations.idiomatic: Yi railed at Lushan, reciting his crimes, then turned to the rebel throng and declared, "Every man must know the difference between loyalty and treason.

sentences.zh: 我死不失節，夫復何恨！」

translations.literal: I die without losing my integrity—what more is there to regret!
translations.idiomatic: I shall die with my honor intact—what is there to regret!"

sentences.zh: □，文水人；

translations.literal: □ was a native of Wenshui.
translations.idiomatic: □ was from Wenshui.

sentences.zh: 奕，懷慎之子；

translations.literal: Yi was Huai Shen's son.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was the son of Lu Huai Shen.

sentences.zh: 清，欽緒之子也。

translations.literal: Qing was Qin Xu's son.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Qing was the son of Jiang Qin Xu.

sentences.zh: 祿山以其黨張萬頃為河南尹。

translations.literal: Lushan appointed his partisan Zhang Wanqing Henan governor.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan installed his follower Zhang Wanqing as governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 封常清帥餘眾至峽，陝郡太守竇廷芝已奔河東，吏民皆散。

translations.literal: Feng Changqing led the survivors to Xia; Shan commandery prefect Dou Tingzhi had already fled to Hedong, and officials and people had all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Changqing led the battered remnant to Xia Pass, but Shan commandery prefect Dou Tingzhi had already fled to Hedong and the officials and populace had melted away.

sentences.zh: 常清謂高仙芝曰：「常清連日血戰，賊鋒不可當。

translations.literal: Changqing said to Gao Xianzhi, "Changqing has fought bloody battles day after day; the rebels' spearhead cannot be withstood.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing told Gao Xianzhi, "I have fought bloody battle after bloody battle—the rebels' assault is unstoppable.

sentences.zh: 且潼關無兵，若賊豕突入關，則長安危矣。

translations.literal: Moreover Tong Pass has no troops; if the rebels charge like boars into the pass, then Chang'an will be in peril.
translations.idiomatic: And Tong Pass stands empty; if the rebels burst through like charging boars, Chang'an itself will be lost.

sentences.zh: 陝不可守，不如引兵先據潼關以拒之。」

translations.literal: Shan cannot be held; better to lead troops first to occupy Tong Pass and resist them there.
translations.idiomatic: We cannot hold Shan—better withdraw now and seize Tong Pass before they do."

sentences.zh: 仙芝乃帥見兵西趣潼關。

translations.literal: Xianzhi then led the troops at hand west toward Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi at once marched west with every man he had left toward Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 賊尋至，官軍狼狽走，無復部伍，士馬相騰踐，死者甚眾。

translations.literal: The rebels soon arrived; the imperial army fled in disarray, no longer in formation, men and horses trampling one another—a great many dead.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels soon caught up; imperial troops fled in chaos, ranks dissolved, horses and men trampling one another—the dead were beyond count.

sentences.zh: 至潼關，修完守備，賊至，不得入而去。

translations.literal: Reaching Tong Pass, they repaired and completed the defenses; when the rebels arrived they could not enter and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Tong Pass they restored the fortifications; when the rebels arrived they could not break through and turned back.

sentences.zh: 祿山使其將崔乾祐屯陝，臨汝、弘農、濟陰、濮陽、雲中郡皆降於祿山。

translations.literal: Lushan had his general Cui Qian You garrison Shan; Linru, Hongnong, Jiyin, Puyang, and Yunzhong commanderies all surrendered to Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan posted Cui Qian You at Shan, while Linru, Hongnong, Jiyin, Puyang, and Yunzhong all submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 是時，朝廷徵兵諸道，皆未至，關中忷懼。

translations.literal: At this time the court was summoning troops from all circuits, but none had yet arrived; within the passes fear and panic spread.
translations.idiomatic: The court had called up troops from every circuit, yet none had arrived; terror gripped the Guanzhong region.

sentences.zh: 會祿山方謀稱帝，留東京不進，故朝廷得為之備，兵亦稍集。

translations.literal: As it happened Lushan was then plotting to declare himself emperor and halted at the Eastern Capital without advancing, so the court was able to prepare, and troops gradually assembled.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune favored the court: Lushan was preparing to declare himself emperor and lingered in the Eastern Capital, giving the government time to regroup as reinforcements slowly gathered.

sentences.zh: 祿山以張通儒之弟通晤為睢陽太守，與陳留長史楊朝宗將胡騎千餘東略地，郡縣官多望風降走，惟東平太守嗣吳王祗、濟南太守李隨起兵拒之。

translations.literal: Lushan appointed Zhang Tongru's younger brother Zhang Tongwu Suiyang prefect; with Chenliu chief administrator Yang Chaozong he led more than a thousand Hu cavalry east to seize territory. Most county and commandery officials fled or surrendered at the rumor of their approach; only Eastern Peace prefect Succeeding Prince of Wu Di and Ji'nan prefect Li Sui raised troops to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan made Zhang Tongwu, younger brother of Zhang Tongru, prefect of Suiyang; with Chenliu chief administrator Yang Chaozong he led a thousand Hu horsemen eastward to conquer the countryside. Officials everywhere surrendered or fled—only Eastern Peace prefect Prince of Wu Di and Ji'nan prefect Li Sui took up arms against them.

sentences.zh: 祗，禕之弟也。

translations.literal: Di was Yi's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Di was the younger brother of Prince Yi.

sentences.zh: 郡縣之不從賊者，皆倚吳王為名。

translations.literal: Commanderies and counties that did not follow the rebels all relied on the Prince of Wu as their rallying name.
translations.idiomatic: Every commandery and county that held out against the rebels did so under the banner of the Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 單父尉賈賁帥吏民南擊睢陽，斬張通晤。

translations.literal: Danfu magistrate Jia Fen led officials and people south to attack Suiyang and beheaded Zhang Tongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Fen, magistrate of Danfu, led local officials and militia south against Suiyang and struck down Zhang Tongwu.

sentences.zh: 李庭望引兵欲東徇地，聞之，不敢進而還。

translations.literal: Li Tingwang was leading troops intending to press east and seize territory; on hearing this he dared not advance and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tingwang, who had been marching east to expand rebel territory, turned back when he heard the news.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以永王璘為山南節度使，江陵長史源洧為之副；

translations.literal: On gengzi, Prince Yong Lin was made Military Commissioner of Shannan, with Jiangling chief administrator Yuan Wei as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Prince Yong Lin was appointed military commissioner of Shannan, with Jiangling chief administrator Yuan Wei as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 穎王□為劍南節度使，蜀郡長史崔圓為之副。

translations.literal: Prince of Ying □ was made Military Commissioner of Jiannan, with Shu commandery chief administrator Cui Yuan as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Ying □ was named military commissioner of Jiannan, with Shu commandery chief administrator Cui Yuan as deputy.

sentences.zh: 二王皆不出閣。

translations.literal: Neither prince left his palace quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Neither prince ever left the palace confines—both appointments were nominal.

sentences.zh: 洧，光裕之子也。

translations.literal: Wei was Guang Yu's son.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Wei was the son of Yuan Guang Yu.

sentences.zh: 上議親征，辛丑，制太子臨國，謂宰相曰：「朕在位垂五十載，倦於憂勤，去秋已欲傳位太子；

translations.literal: The emperor considered a personal campaign; on xinchou he ordered the crown prince to oversee the state and told the chief councillors, "I have reigned for nearly fifty years and am weary of constant worry and labor; last autumn I already wished to pass the throne to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor contemplated leading the army himself; on xinchou he decreed that the crown prince would govern in his stead and told his chief ministers, "Near fifty years on the throne have wearied me with ceaseless care; as early as last autumn I meant to abdicate in favor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 值水旱相仍，不欲以餘災遺子孫，淹留俟稍豐。

translations.literal: Calamities of flood and drought followed one after another, and I did not wish to bequeath lingering disaster to posterity; I delayed, waiting until things grew somewhat richer.
translations.idiomatic: Floods and drought struck in succession, and I refused to leave such misfortune as my legacy—I stayed on, waiting for better days.

sentences.zh: 不意逆胡橫發，朕當親征，且使之監國。

translations.literal: I did not expect the rebel barbarian to rise violently; I shall campaign in person and for the meantime have him supervise the realm.
translations.idiomatic: I never imagined the rebel would erupt so suddenly; I must take the field myself and leave him to govern the realm in my absence.

sentences.zh: 事平之日，朕將高枕無為矣。」

translations.literal: When affairs are settled, I shall at last rest easy with pillows high and have no further tasks.
translations.idiomatic: When peace returns, I shall finally lay down the burden and rest."

sentences.zh: 楊國忠大懼，退謂韓、虢、秦三夫人曰：「太子素惡吾家專橫久矣，若一旦得天下，吾與姊妹並命在旦暮矣！」
