translations.literal: Yang Guozhong was greatly afraid; withdrawing, he said to the Ladies of Han, Guo, and Qin, "The crown prince has long hated our family's overbearing ways; if he one day gains the realm, my sisters and I will have but a day or a morning to live!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong was terrified. He withdrew and told the Ladies of Han, Guo, and Qin, "The crown prince has hated our family's arrogance for years—if he ever takes the throne, my sisters and I are dead by morning!"

sentences.zh: 相與聚哭，使三夫人說貴妃，銜土請命於上；

translations.literal: Together they gathered and wept, and had the three ladies persuade the Noble Consort to beg the emperor for their lives, mouths filled with earth in supplication.
translations.idiomatic: They wept together and sent the three ladies to plead with the Noble Consort, who in turn begged the emperor on bended knee as though holding earth in her mouth.

sentences.zh: 事遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was thereupon dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was quietly abandoned.

sentences.zh: 顏真卿召募勇士，旬日至萬餘人，諭以舉兵討安祿山，繼以涕泣，士皆感憤。

translations.literal: Yan Zhenqing recruited brave warriors; within ten days more than ten thousand arrived. He urged them to raise troops to punish An Lushan, and followed with weeping; the soldiers were all moved to indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing raised a force of brave men; within ten days more than ten thousand had gathered. He called on them to take up arms against An Lushan, weeping as he spoke, and every man burned with righteous fury.

sentences.zh: 祿山使其黨段子光繼李□、盧奕、蔣清首徇河北諸郡，至平原，壬寅，真卿執子光，腰斬以徇；

translations.literal: Lushan had his partisan Duan Ziguang carry the heads of Li □, Lu Yi, and Jiang Qing through the Hebei commanderies as a warning; reaching Pingyuan, on renyin Zhenqing seized Ziguang and cut him in two at the waist as a public example.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan sent his follower Duan Ziguang to parade the heads of Li □, Lu Yi, and Jiang Qing through Hebei as a warning; when he reached Pingyuan on renyin, Zhenqing seized him and had him cut in half at the waist for all to see.

sentences.zh: 取三人首，續以蒲身，棺斂葬之，祭哭受吊。

translations.literal: He took the three men's heads, attached rush bodies to them, coffined and buried them, and offered sacrifices and mourning while receiving condolences.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered the three heads, fashioned rush bodies to complete the corpses, gave them proper burial, and mourned them with rites while accepting the condolences of the people.

sentences.zh: 祿山以海運使劉道玄攝景城太守，清池尉賈載、鹽山尉河內穆寧共斬道玄，得其甲仗五十餘船；

translations.literal: Lushan had maritime transport commissioner Liu Daoxuan act as acting Jingcheng prefect; Qingchi magistrate Jia Zai, Yanshan magistrate Mu Ning of Henei, and others jointly beheaded Daoxuan and seized more than fifty boats of armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan had placed maritime transport commissioner Liu Daoxuan in charge of Jingcheng; magistrate Jia Zai of Qingchi and magistrate Mu Ning of Yanshan in Henei joined forces to kill Daoxuan and capture more than fifty boatloads of arms and armor.

sentences.zh: 攜道玄首謁長史李□，□收嚴莊宗族，悉誅之。

translations.literal: Carrying Daoxuan's head they went to see chief administrator Li □; □ seized the Yan Zhuang clan and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: They brought Daoxuan's head to chief administrator Li □, who rounded up the entire clan of Yan Zhuang and put them all to death.

sentences.zh: 是日，送道玄首至平原，真卿召載、寧及清河尉張澹詣平原計事。

translations.literal: That same day they sent Daoxuan's head to Pingyuan; Zhenqing summoned Zai, Ning, and Qinghe magistrate Zhang Tan to Pingyuan to plan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Daoxuan's head reached Pingyuan; Zhenqing called together Zai, Ning, and Qinghe magistrate Zhang Tan to counsel on strategy.

sentences.zh: 饒陽太守盧全誠據城不受代；

translations.literal: Raoyang prefect Lu Quancheng held the city and would not accept replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Raoyang prefect Lu Quancheng held his city and refused to yield to the rebel appointee.

sentences.zh: 河間司法李奐殺祿山所署長史王懷忠；

translations.literal: Hejian judicial officer Li Huan killed Wang Huaizhong, the chief administrator Lushan had appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan, judicial officer of Hejian, killed Wang Huaizhong, the chief administrator Lushan had installed.

sentences.zh: 李隨遣游弈將訾嗣賢濟河，殺祿山所署博平太守馬冀；

translations.literal: Li Sui sent roaming inspector Zi Sixian across the river and killed Ma Ji, the Boping prefect Lushan had appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sui sent roaming inspector Zi Sixian across the Yellow River to kill Ma Ji, Lushan's appointee as prefect of Boping.

sentences.zh: 各有眾數千或萬人，共推真卿為盟主，軍事皆稟焉。

translations.literal: Each had followers numbering several thousand or ten thousand; together they made Zhenqing alliance leader, and all military affairs were referred to him.
translations.idiomatic: Each commanded thousands or even ten thousand men; together they chose Zhenqing as their alliance chief, and every military decision passed through him.

sentences.zh: 祿山使張獻誠將上谷、博陵、常山、趙郡、文安五郡團結兵萬人圍饒陽。

translations.literal: Lushan sent Zhang Xiancheng to lead ten thousand militia from the five commanderies of Shanggu, Boling, Changshan, Zhao, and Wen'an to besiege Raoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan dispatched Zhang Xiancheng with ten thousand levies from Shanggu, Boling, Changshan, Zhao, and Wen'an to lay siege to Raoyang.

sentences.zh: 高仙芝之東征也，監軍邊令誠數以事幹之，仙芝多不從。

translations.literal: When Gao Xianzhi marched east, army supervisor Bian Lingcheng repeatedly interfered in affairs, and Xianzhi mostly did not follow him.
translations.idiomatic: During Gao Xianzhi's eastern campaign, army supervisor Bian Lingcheng meddled at every turn, and Xianzhi largely ignored him.

sentences.zh: 令誠入奏事，具言仙芝、常清橈敗之狀，且云：「常清以賊搖眾，而仙芝棄陝地數百里，又盜減軍士糧賜。」

translations.literal: Lingcheng entered to memorialize the throne and fully reported Xianzhi's and Changqing's routed defeats, saying moreover, "Changqing exaggerated the rebels to shake the troops, while Xianzhi abandoned several hundred li of Shan territory, and also stole and reduced the soldiers' grain and rewards."
translations.idiomatic: Lingcheng went to court and laid out the full story of Xianzhi's and Changqing's routs, adding, "Changqing inflated the rebel threat to panic the army, while Xianzhi abandoned hundreds of li in Shan—and embezzled the soldiers' rations and pay besides."

sentences.zh: 上大怒，癸卯，遣令誠繼敕即軍中斬仙芝及常清。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered; on guimao he sent Lingcheng with follow-up edicts to execute Xianzhi and Changqing immediately in the army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage; on guimao he dispatched Lingcheng with orders to behead Xianzhi and Changqing on the spot in camp.

sentences.zh: 初，常清既敗，三遣使奉表陳賊形勢，上皆不之見。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Changqing was defeated, he three times sent envoys bearing memorials describing the rebels' situation, and the emperor would not receive them.
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat Changqing had three times sent memorials detailing the rebel threat, and the emperor refused even to read them.

sentences.zh: 常清乃自馳詣闕，至渭南，敕削其官爵，令還仙芝軍，白衣自效。

translations.literal: Changqing then rode in person to the palace; reaching Weinan, an edict stripped him of rank and title and ordered him back to Xianzhi's army to serve in plain clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing then galloped to court himself; at Weinan an edict stripped him of rank and sent him back to Xianzhi's army in commoner's dress to redeem himself.

sentences.zh: 常清草遺表曰：「臣死之後，望陛下不輕此賊，無忘臣言！」

translations.literal: Changqing drafted a final memorial saying, "After your servant dies, I hope Your Majesty will not underestimate this rebel, and will not forget your servant's words!"
translations.idiomatic: Changqing wrote a death memorial: "When I am gone, Your Majesty, do not take this rebel lightly—and do not forget what I tell you now!"

sentences.zh: 時朝議皆以為祿山狂悖，不日授首，故常清云然。

translations.literal: At the time court opinion universally held that Lushan was mad and rebellious and would within days lose his head, and so Changqing spoke thus.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion then held that Lushan was a reckless madman who would be beheaded any day—which was why Changqing wrote as he did.

sentences.zh: 令誠至潼關，先引常清，宣敕示之；

translations.literal: Lingcheng reached Tong Pass, first brought out Changqing, and displayed the edict to him.
translations.idiomatic: Lingcheng arrived at Tong Pass and first summoned Changqing to read the imperial decree.

sentences.zh: 常清以表附令誠上之。

translations.literal: Changqing attached the memorial and had Lingcheng submit it.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing handed his memorial to Lingcheng to deliver to the throne.

sentences.zh: 常清既死，陳屍蘧蒢。

translations.literal: After Changqing died, his corpse was displayed on coarse matting.
translations.idiomatic: After Changqing was killed, his body was laid out on a straw mat for all to see.

sentences.zh: 仙芝還，至聽事，令誠索陌刀手百餘人自隨，乃謂仙芝曰：「大夫亦有恩命。」

translations.literal: Xianzhi returned and reached the audience hall; Lingcheng summoned more than a hundred saber troops to accompany him, then said to Xianzhi, "The Grand Marshal also has an imperial command."
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi returned to headquarters; Lingcheng appeared with more than a hundred saber-wielding executioners at his back and told Xianzhi, "You have an edict as well, Grand Marshal."

sentences.zh: 仙芝遽下，令誠宣敕。

translations.literal: Xianzhi hurriedly descended; Lingcheng proclaimed the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi stepped down at once; Lingcheng read the decree aloud.

sentences.zh: 仙芝曰：「我遇敵而退，死則宜矣。

translations.literal: Xianzhi said, "I met the enemy and retreated—death is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi said, "I retreated before the enemy—if I must die, so be it.

sentences.zh: 今上戴天，下履地，謂我盜減糧賜則誣也。」

translations.literal: Now above I bear heaven, below I tread earth—to say I stole and reduced grain and rewards is slander.
translations.idiomatic: I stand under heaven and upon the earth—the charge that I stole the soldiers' rations is a lie."

sentences.zh: 時士卒在前，皆大呼稱枉，其聲振地；

translations.literal: At the time soldiers were in front and all shouted that he was wronged; the sound shook the earth.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers massed before him, roaring that he had been wronged until the ground itself seemed to shake.

sentences.zh: 遂斬之，以將軍李承光攝領其眾。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was beheaded, and General Li Chengguang was appointed acting commander of the force.
translations.idiomatic: He was beheaded on the spot, and General Li Chengguang was placed in temporary command of the army.

sentences.zh: 河西、隴右節度使哥舒翰病廢在家，上藉其威名，且素與祿山不協，召見，拜兵馬副元帥，將兵八萬以討祿山；

translations.literal: Hexi and Longyou Military Commissioner Geshu Han was ill and disabled at home; the emperor relied on his formidable reputation and also knew he had long been at odds with Lushan, summoned and saw him, appointed him Vice Marshal of armies and cavalry, and sent eighty thousand troops to punish Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: Geshu Han, military commissioner of Hexi and Longyou, lay ill and infirm at home; the emperor, trusting in his renown and knowing his old enmity with Lushan, summoned him, made him vice marshal of armies and cavalry, and gave him eighty thousand men to crush the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 仍敕天下四面進兵，會攻洛陽。

translations.literal: He also ordered troops from all four quarters to advance together and jointly attack Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He also decreed a converging attack on Luoyang from every direction.

sentences.zh: 翰以病固辭，上不許，以田良丘為御史中丞，充行軍司馬，起居郎蕭昕為判官，蕃將火拔歸仁等各將部落以從，並仙芝舊卒，號二十萬，軍於潼關。

translations.literal: Han because of illness firmly declined, but the emperor would not permit it; Tian Liangqiu was made Censor-in-Chief and acting army secretary; Palace Attendant Xiao Xin was made adjutant; tribal generals Huoba Guiren and others each led their clans to follow; together with Xianzhi's old troops they numbered two hundred thousand, and the army encamped at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Han pleaded illness and refused, but the emperor would not hear of it. Tian Liangqiu became censor-in-chief and army secretary; palace attendant Xiao Xin served as adjutant; tribal commanders such as Huoba Guiren brought their warriors; together with Xianzhi's veterans they mustered two hundred thousand men and encamped at Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 翰病，不能治事，悉以軍政委田良丘；

translations.literal: Han was ill and could not manage affairs; he entirely entrusted military matters to Tian Liangqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Geshu Han was too ill to command; he delegated all military authority to Tian Liangqiu.

sentences.zh: 良丘復不敢專決，使王思禮主騎，李承光主步，二人爭長，無所統一。

translations.literal: Liangqiu in turn dared not decide alone, and had Wang Sili command the cavalry and Li Chengguang command the infantry; the two contended for seniority and nothing was unified.
translations.idiomatic: But Liangqiu dared make no decision on his own, splitting command between Wang Sili for cavalry and Li Chengguang for infantry—two rivals with no unified leadership.

sentences.zh: 翰用法嚴而不恤，士卒皆懈弛，無鬥志。

translations.literal: Han applied the law strictly without compassion; the soldiers all grew slack and had no fighting will.
translations.idiomatic: Han enforced discipline with pitiless severity; morale collapsed and the men lost all will to fight.

sentences.zh: 安祿山大同軍使高秀巖寇振武軍，朔方節度使郭子儀擊敗之，子儀乘勝拔靜邊軍。

translations.literal: An Lushan's Datong Army commissioner Gao Xiuyan raided Zhenwu Army; Shuofang Military Commissioner Guo Ziyi defeated him, and Ziyi pressed the victory to take Jingbian Army.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan's Datong army commissioner Gao Xiuyan struck at Zhenwu Army; Guo Ziyi, military commissioner of Shuofang, routed him and drove on to capture Jingbian Army.

sentences.zh: 大同兵馬使薛忠義寇靜邊軍，子儀使左兵馬使李光弼、右兵馬使高浚、左武鋒使僕固懷恩、右武鋒使渾釋之等逆擊，大破之，坑其騎七千。

translations.literal: Datong army horse commissioner Xue Zhongyi raided Jingbian Army; Ziyi sent Left Army Horse Commissioner Li Guangbi, Right Army Horse Commissioner Gao Jun, Left Vanguard Commissioner Pugu Huai'en, Right Vanguard Commissioner Hun Shizhi, and others to meet and strike them, thoroughly defeating them and burying alive seven thousand of their cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Datong cavalry commander Xue Zhongyi attacked Jingbian Army; Guo Ziyi sent Li Guangbi, Gao Jun, Pugu Huai'en, Hun Shizhi, and others to intercept them, crushing the rebel force and burying seven thousand horsemen alive.

sentences.zh: 進圍雲中，使別將公孫瓊巖將二千騎擊馬邑，拔之，開東陘關。

translations.literal: He advanced to besiege Yunzhong, sent another general Gongsun Qiongyan with two thousand cavalry to strike Mayi, took it, and opened Dongxing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to besiege Yunzhong, dispatched Gongsun Qiongyan with two thousand horsemen to seize Mayi, and reopened Dongxing Pass.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，加子儀御史大夫。

translations.literal: On jiachen Ziyi was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen Guo Ziyi was promoted to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 懷恩，哥濫拔延之曾孫也，世為金微都督。

translations.literal: Huai'en was the great-grandson of Gelan Bayan; for generations his family had been jiedu of Jinwei.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en was great-grandson of Gelan Bayan; his family had held the Jinwei governorship for generations.

sentences.zh: 釋之，渾部酋長，世為皋蘭都督。

translations.literal: Shizhi was a chieftain of the Hun tribe; for generations his family had been jiedu of Gao Lan.
translations.idiomatic: Hun Shizhi was a chieftain of the Hun people; his clan had governed Gao Lan for generations.

sentences.zh: 顏杲卿將起兵，參軍馮虔、前真定令賈深、蒿城尉崔安石、郡人翟萬德、內丘丞張通幽等皆預其謀；

translations.literal: Yan Gaoqing was about to raise troops; staff officer Feng Qian, former Zhending magistrate Jia Shen, Haocheng magistrate Cui Anshi, local man Zhai Wande, Neiqiu assistant magistrate Zhang Tongyou, and others all took part in the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Gaoqing prepared to rise in arms; staff officer Feng Qian, former magistrate Jia Shen of Zhending, magistrate Cui Anshi of Haocheng, local leader Zhai Wande, Neiqiu assistant magistrate Zhang Tongyou, and others all joined the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 又遣人語太原尹王承業，密與相應。

translations.literal: He also sent word to Taiyuan governor Wang Chengye to respond in secret coordination.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent secret word to Taiyuan governor Wang Chengye, urging him to act in concert.

sentences.zh: 會顏真卿自平原遣杲卿甥盧逖潛告杲卿，欲連兵斷祿山歸路，以緩其西入之謀。

translations.literal: As it happened Yan Zhenqing from Pingyuan sent Gaoqing's nephew Lu Su by a hidden route to inform Gaoqing, wishing to join forces and cut off Lushan's line of retreat, thereby slowing his plan to drive west.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Yan Zhenqing sent Gaoqing's nephew Lu Su by a secret route from Pingyuan with word that they should unite to sever Lushan's retreat and delay his westward advance.

sentences.zh: 時祿山遣其金吾將軍高邈詣幽州徵兵，未還，杲卿以祿山命召李欽湊，使帥眾詣群受犒賚；

translations.literal: At the time Lushan had sent his Gold Crow Guard general Gao Miao to Youzhou to levy troops and he had not yet returned; Gaoqing used Lushan's order to summon Li Qincou and had him lead his troops to the commandery to receive rewards and bounty.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan had sent Gold Crow Guard general Gao Miao to Youzhou to raise troops and had not yet returned; Gaoqing forged Lushan's summons for Li Qincou and had him march his men to the commandery to collect their reward.

sentences.zh: 丙午，薄暮，欽湊至，杲卿使袁履謙、馮虔等攜酒食妓樂往勞之，並其黨皆大醉，乃斷欽湊首，收其甲兵，盡縛其黨，明日，斬之，悉散井陘之眾。

translations.literal: On bingwu, near dusk, Qincou arrived; Gaoqing had Yuan Lüqian, Feng Qian, and others carry wine, food, and singing girls to entertain them, and Qincou and his partisans all became greatly drunk; then they cut off Qincou's head, seized his armor and weapons, bound all his followers, and the next day beheaded them and fully dispersed the garrison at Jingxing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu at dusk Li Qincou arrived; Gaoqing sent Yuan Lüqian and Feng Qian with wine, feasts, and entertainers to welcome him. Qincou and his men drank themselves senseless; Gaoqing's men struck off Qincou's head, seized their arms, bound the rest, executed them the next day, and scattered the garrison at Jingxing Pass.

sentences.zh: 有頃，高邈自幽州還，且至蒿城，杲卿使馮虔往擒之。

translations.literal: Before long Gao Miao returned from Youzhou and was about to reach Haocheng; Gaoqing sent Feng Qian to capture him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Gao Miao returned from Youzhou and was nearing Haocheng; Gaoqing dispatched Feng Qian to take him.

sentences.zh: 南境又白何千年自東京來，崔安石與崔萬德馳詣醴泉驛迎千年，又擒之，同日致於郡下。

translations.literal: The southern frontier also reported that He Qiannian was coming from the Eastern Capital; Cui Anshi and Cui Wande galloped to Lichuan Post to welcome Qiannian, and captured him too; on the same day both were delivered below the commandery seat.
translations.idiomatic: Word came from the south that He Qiannian was marching from the Eastern Capital; Cui Anshi and Cui Wande rode out to Lichuan Post to greet him—and seized him as well. Both prisoners reached the commandery capital that same day.

sentences.zh: 千年謂杲卿曰：「今太守欲輸力王室，既善其始，當慎其終。

translations.literal: Qiannian said to Gaoqing, "Now the prefect wishes to exert strength for the royal house; since you have made a good beginning, you should be careful at the end.
translations.idiomatic: He Qiannian told Gaoqing, "You mean to serve the throne—that is well begun. See that you finish as wisely as you start.

sentences.zh: 此郡應募烏合，難以臨敵，宜深溝高壘，勿與爭鋒。

translations.literal: This commandery's recruited rabble is hard to face the enemy; you should dig deep moats and raise high ramparts, and not contend for the sharp edge.
translations.idiomatic: The men this commandery has mustered are a disorderly mob, unfit to meet the enemy in the field; dig deep moats, raise high walls, and do not try to win the first clash.

sentences.zh: 俟朔方軍至，並力齊進，傳檄趙、魏、斷燕、薊要膂，彼則成擒矣。

translations.literal: Wait until the Shuofang army arrives, join strength and advance together, send proclamations to Zhao and Wei, cut the vital spine of Yan and Ji, and they will then be captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: Wait for the Shuofang army to arrive, then advance in concert; issue proclamations across Zhao and Wei and sever the rebel lifeline through Yan and Ji—and they will be taken alive.

sentences.zh: 今且宜聲云『李光弼引步騎一萬出井陘』，因使人說張獻誠云：『足下所將多團練之人，無堅甲利兵，難以當山西勁兵』，獻誠必解圍遁去。

translations.literal: For now you should proclaim aloud, 'Li Guangbi is leading ten thousand infantry and cavalry out through Jingxing Pass,' and then send someone to tell Zhang Xiancheng, 'Those under your command are mostly militia men, without stout armor or sharp weapons, and can hardly stand against Shanxi crack troops'—Xiancheng will surely lift the siege and flee.
translations.idiomatic: For the moment, spread word that Li Guangbi is marching ten thousand foot and horse out of Jingxing Pass, then send an envoy to Zhang Xiancheng: 'Your force is mostly local militia, poorly armed—they cannot stand against the hard fighters of Shanxi.' Xiancheng will lift the siege and run.

sentences.zh: 此亦一奇也。」

translations.literal: This too is one stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: That too would be a bold stroke."

sentences.zh: 杲卿悅，用其策，獻誠果遁去，其團練兵皆潰。

translations.literal: Gaoqing was pleased and used his plan; Xiancheng indeed fled, and his militia troops all collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing was delighted and adopted the plan. Xiancheng fled as predicted, and his militia scattered in rout.

sentences.zh: 杲卿乃使人入饒陽城，慰勞將士。

translations.literal: Gaoqing then sent men into Raoyang city to comfort and reward the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing then sent envoys into Raoyang to hearten the garrison.

sentences.zh: 命崔安石等徇諸郡云：「大軍已下井陘，朝夕當至，先平河北諸郡。

translations.literal: He ordered Cui Anshi and others to proclaim through the commanderies, saying, 'The great army has already descended Jingxing Pass and will arrive within days; it will first pacify the Hebei commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He had Cui Anshi and others ride through the commanderies proclaiming: 'The main army has already come down through Jingxing Pass and will arrive within days—Hebei will be pacified first.

sentences.zh: 先下者賞，後至者誅！」

translations.literal: Those who submit first will be rewarded; those who come late will be executed!'
translations.idiomatic: Submit first and be rewarded; hold out and be put to death!'

sentences.zh: 於是河北諸郡響應，凡十七郡皆歸朝廷，兵合二十餘萬；

translations.literal: Thereupon the Hebei commanderies responded; in all seventeen commanderies returned to the court, and troops totaled more than two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At that, commanderies across Hebei answered the call; seventeen in all returned to the throne, and their combined strength exceeded two hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 其附祿山者，惟范陽、盧龍、密雲、漁陽、汲、鄴六郡而已。

translations.literal: Those attached to Lushan were only the six commanderies of Fanyang, Lulong, Miyun, Yuyang, Ji, and Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Only six commanderies still held for Lushan: Fanyang, Lulong, Miyun, Yuyang, Ji, and Ye.

sentences.zh: 杲卿又密使人入漁陽招賈循，郟城人馬燧說循曰：「祿山負恩悖逆，雖得洛陽，終歸夷滅。

translations.literal: Gaoqing again secretly sent men into Yuyang to win over Jia Xun; Jia Cheng native Ma Sui said to Xun, 'Lushan has betrayed grace and rebelled; though he has taken Luoyang, in the end he will be exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing also sent secret envoys to Yuyang to recruit Jia Xun. Ma Sui of Jia Cheng urged him: 'Lushan has betrayed the throne; though he holds Luoyang now, he will be destroyed in the end.

sentences.zh: 公若誅諸將之不從命者，以范陽歸國，傾其根柢，此不世之功也。」

translations.literal: If you execute the generals who do not obey orders and return Fanyang to the state, overturning his root foundation—this is an achievement not of a single age.'
translations.idiomatic: If you kill the officers who refuse your orders and return Fanyang to the dynasty, you will uproot the rebellion at its source—a feat for the ages.'

sentences.zh: 循然之，猶豫不時發。

translations.literal: Xun assented to this, yet hesitated and did not act in time.
translations.idiomatic: Xun agreed, but hesitated and never moved when he should have.

sentences.zh: 別將牛潤容知之，以告祿山，祿山使其黨韓朝陽召循。

translations.literal: Separate general Niu Runrong learned of it and told Lushan; Lushan had his partisan Han Chaoyang summon Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commander Niu Runrong learned of the plot and informed Lushan, who sent his follower Han Chaoyang to summon Xun.

sentences.zh: 朝陽至漁陽，引循屏語，使壯士縊殺之，滅其族；

translations.literal: Chaoyang reached Yuyang, drew Xun aside for private speech, and had stalwart men strangle and kill him, exterminating his clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Chaoyang reached Yuyang he drew Xun aside for a private word, then had strong men strangle him and wiped out his entire family.

sentences.zh: 以別將牛廷玠知范陽軍事。

translations.literal: He made separate general Niu Tingjie know Fanyang military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He put deputy commander Niu Tingjie in charge of Fanyang's military affairs.

sentences.zh: 史思明、李立節將蕃、漢步騎萬人擊博陵、常山。

translations.literal: Shi Siming and Li Lijie led ten thousand barbarian and Han infantry and cavalry to attack Boling and Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming and Li Lijie marched ten thousand mixed barbarian and Han foot and horse against Boling and Changshan.

sentences.zh: 馬燧亡入西山；

translations.literal: Ma Sui fled and entered the Western Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui fled into the Western Mountains.

sentences.zh: 隱者徐遇匿之，得免。

translations.literal: Recluse Xu Yu hid him, and he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The hermit Xu Yu sheltered him, and he survived.

sentences.zh: 初，祿山自將欲攻潼關，至新安，聞河北有變而還。

translations.literal: Earlier, Lushan personally commanded and wished to attack Tong Pass; reaching Xin'an, he heard there was trouble in Hebei and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Lushan had led his army in person toward Tong Pass; when he reached Xin'an and heard that Hebei had risen against him, he turned back.

sentences.zh: 蔡希德將兵萬人自河內北擊常山。

translations.literal: Cai Xide led ten thousand troops from Henei north to strike Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xide led ten thousand men north from Henei to attack Changshan.

sentences.zh: 戊申，榮王琬薨，贈謚靖恭太子。

translations.literal: On wushen, Prince Rong Wan died; he was posthumously given the title Prince Jinggong.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Prince Rong Wan died and was posthumously honored as Prince Jinggong.

sentences.zh: 是歲，吐蕃贊普乞梨蘇籠獵贊卒，子娑悉籠獵贊立。

translations.literal: This year the Tibetan tsenpo Qili Sulungliezan died, and his son Suoxi Sulungliezan was enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Tibetan emperor Qili Sulungliezan died, and his son Suoxi Sulungliezan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 肅宗文明武德大聖大宣孝皇帝上之上

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong of Tang, Cultured, Martial, Virtuous, Great Sage, Great Proclaimer of Filial Piety—Upper Part of the Upper Scroll
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong of Tang, Upper Part of the Upper Scroll

sentences.zh: 玄宗至道大聖大明孝皇帝下之下至德元年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong of Tang, Latter Part of the Lower Scroll, Zhide year 1 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong of Tang, Latter Part of the Lower Scroll, Zhide year 1 (

sentences.zh: 丙申，公元七五六年）

translations.literal: bingshen, AD 756)
translations.idiomatic: bingshen, AD 756)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙卯朔，祿山自稱大燕皇帝，改元聖武，以達奚珣為侍中，張通儒為中書令，高尚、嚴莊為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the yimao new moon, Lushan styled himself Emperor of Great Yan, changed the era name to Shengwu, made Daxi Xun Palace Attendant, Zhang Tongru Director of the Secretariat, and Gao Shang and Yan Zhuang Vice Directors of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the yimao new moon, Lushan declared himself Emperor of Great Yan and adopted the era name Shengwu. He made Daxi Xun Palace Attendant, Zhang Tongru Director of the Secretariat, and Gao Shang and Yan Zhuang Vice Directors of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 李隨至睢陽，有眾數萬。

translations.literal: Li Sui reached Suiyang and had a host of several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sui reached Suiyang at the head of several tens of thousands of men.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，以隨為河南節度使，以前高要尉許遠為睢陽太守兼防禦使。

translations.literal: On bingchen Li Sui was made Henan military commissioner, and former Gaoyao magistrate Xu Yuan was made Suiyang prefect concurrently defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Li Sui was appointed Henan military commissioner, and the former magistrate of Gaoyao, Xu Yuan, was made prefect of Suiyang and defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 濮陽客尚衡起兵討祿山，以郡人王棲曜為衙前總管，攻拔濟陰，殺祿山將邢超然。

translations.literal: Puyang guest Shang Heng raised troops to punish Lushan, made commandery man Wang Qiyao yamen front commander, attacked and took Jiyin, and killed Lushan's general Xing Chaoran.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Heng of Puyang took up arms against Lushan, made the local man Wang Qiyao his front commander, captured Jiyin, and killed Lushan's general Xing Chaoran.

sentences.zh: 顏杲卿使其子泉明、賈深、翟萬德獻李欽湊首及何千年、高邈於京師。

translations.literal: Yan Gaoqing sent his son Quanming, Jia Shen, and Zhai Wande to present Li Qincou's head and He Qiannian and Gao Miao to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Gaoqing sent his son Quanming, together with Jia Shen and Zhai Wande, to the capital with Li Qincou's head and the captives He Qiannian and Gao Miao.

sentences.zh: 張通幽泣請曰：「通幽兄陷賊，乞與泉明偕行，以救宗族。」

translations.literal: Zhang Tongyou wept and requested, saying, 'Tongyou's elder brother is trapped among the rebels; I beg to travel together with Quanming to save my clan.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tongyou wept and pleaded: 'My elder brother is trapped with the rebels—let me go with Quanming to save our family.'

sentences.zh: 杲卿哀而許之。

translations.literal: Gaoqing pitied him and consented.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, Gaoqing granted his request.

sentences.zh: 至太原，通幽欲自托於王承業，乃教之留泉明等，更其表，多自為功，毀短杲卿，別遣使獻之。

translations.literal: Reaching Taiyuan, Tongyou wished to attach himself to Wang Chengye, and so taught him to detain Quanming and the others, alter the memorial, claim much merit for himself, speak ill of Gaoqing, and send a separate envoy to present it.
translations.idiomatic: At Taiyuan, Tongyou sought favor with Wang Chengye. He persuaded Chengye to hold Quanming and the others, rewrite the memorial to credit himself, slander Gaoqing, and send a separate envoy to present the trophies.

sentences.zh: 杲卿起兵才八日，守備未完，史思明、蔡希德引兵皆至城下。

translations.literal: Gaoqing had raised troops only eight days; defenses were not yet complete when Shi Siming and Cai Xide led troops, all arriving below the city.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing had been in arms only eight days and his defenses were still unfinished when Shi Siming and Cai Xide marched up and encamped beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 杲卿告急於承業。

translations.literal: Gaoqing reported urgency to Chengye.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing sent urgent appeals to Chengye for relief.

sentences.zh: 承業既竊其功，利於城陷，遂擁兵不救。

translations.literal: Chengye, having already stolen his merit, benefited from the city's fall, and so held his troops and did not rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye had already stolen the credit and stood to gain if the city fell, so he kept his army idle and refused to help.

sentences.zh: 杲卿晝夜拒戰，糧盡矢竭；

translations.literal: Gaoqing resisted day and night; grain was exhausted and arrows spent.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing fought on day and night until food ran out and arrows were gone.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，城陷。

translations.literal: On renxu the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu the city fell.

sentences.zh: 賊縱兵殺萬餘人，執杲卿及袁履謙等送洛陽。

translations.literal: The rebels released troops and killed more than ten thousand men, seized Gaoqing and Yuan Lüqian and others, and sent them to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels slaughtered more than ten thousand people, seized Gaoqing, Yuan Lüqian, and the rest, and sent them to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 王承業使者至京師，玄宗大喜，拜承業羽林大將軍，麾下受官爵者以百數。

translations.literal: Wang Chengye's envoy reached the capital; Emperor Xuanzong was greatly pleased, appointed Chengye General of the Feathered Forest, and those under his command receiving offices and ranks numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chengye's envoy reached the capital, Emperor Xuanzong was overjoyed. He made Chengye General of the Feathered Forest and ennobled hundreds of his followers.

sentences.zh: 征顏杲卿為衛尉卿，朝命未至，常山已陷。

translations.literal: Yan Gaoqing was summoned as Minister of the Guard for the Emperor; the court order had not yet arrived when Changshan already fell.
translations.idiomatic: The court summoned Yan Gaoqing to be Minister of the Guard for the Emperor, but the decree had not yet arrived when Changshan fell.

sentences.zh: 杲卿至洛陽，祿山數之曰：「汝自范陽戶曹，我奏汝為判官，不數年超至太守，何負於汝而反邪？」

translations.literal: When Gaoqing reached Luoyang, Lushan reproached him, saying, 'You were only a Fanyang household-section clerk; I memorialized you as aide, and within a few years you rose above to prefect—what did I fail to give you that you rebel?'
translations.idiomatic: When Gaoqing reached Luoyang, Lushan berated him: 'You were a mere clerk in Fanyang; I had you made my aide and within a few years raised you to prefect. What did I ever do to you that you turned against me?'

sentences.zh: 杲卿瞋目罵曰：「汝本營州牧羊羯奴，天子擢汝為三道節度使，恩幸無比，何負於汝而反？

translations.literal: Gaoqing glared and cursed, saying, 'You were originally a Jie slave herding sheep in Yingzhou; the Son of Heaven promoted you to commissioner of three circuits, with favor unmatched—what did he fail to give you that you rebel?
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing glared and shouted back: 'You were a Jie shepherd-slave from Yingzhou! The Son of Heaven made you commissioner of three circuits and favored you beyond measure—what did he ever do to you that you rebelled?

sentences.zh: 我世為唐臣，祿位皆唐有，雖為汝所奏，豈從汝反邪！

translations.literal: My family for generations has been Tang subjects; salary and rank all belong to Tang—though you memorialized me, how could I follow you in rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: My family has served Tang for generations; every rank I hold comes from the throne. You may have recommended me, but I would never follow you in rebellion!

sentences.zh: 我為國討賊，恨不斬汝，何謂反也！

translations.literal: I am punishing rebels for the state; I regret only that I did not behead you—how can you call this rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: I took up arms to destroy a traitor to the realm—I only regret that I did not cut off your head. How dare you call me a rebel!

sentences.zh: 臊羯狗，何不速殺我！」

translations.literal: Stinking Jie dog—why not quickly kill me!'
translations.idiomatic: Filthy Jie cur—kill me now!'

sentences.zh: 祿山大怒，並袁履謙等縛於中橋之柱而冎之。

translations.literal: Lushan was greatly enraged, and together with Yuan Lüqian and others bound them to the pillars of the Central Bridge and dismembered them.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan flew into a rage, had them bound to the pillars of the Central Bridge together with Yuan Lüqian and the others, and cut them to pieces.

sentences.zh: 杲卿、履謙比死，罵不虛口。

translations.literal: Gaoqing and Lüqian faced death together, cursing without an idle mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing and Lüqian went to their deaths side by side, cursing without pause.

sentences.zh: 顏氏一門死於刀鋸者三十餘人。

translations.literal: Of the Yan clan, more than thirty persons died by blade and saw.
translations.idiomatic: More than thirty members of the Yan clan died by the executioner's blade.

sentences.zh: 史思明、李立節、蔡希德既克常山，引兵擊諸郡之不從者，所過殘滅，於是鄴、廣平、巨鹿、趙、上谷、博陵、文安、魏、信都等郡復為賊守。

translations.literal: Shi Siming, Li Lijie, and Cai Xide, having taken Changshan, led troops to strike commanderies that did not submit; wherever they passed they ravaged and destroyed, and thereupon Ye, Guangping, Julu, Zhao, Shanggu, Boling, Wen'an, Wei, Xindu, and other commanderies again became rebel-held.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Siming, Li Lijie, and Cai Xide captured Changshan, they marched against every commandery that still held out, leaving devastation in their wake. Ye, Guangping, Julu, Zhao, Shanggu, Boling, Wen'an, Wei, Xindu, and others fell back into rebel hands.

sentences.zh: 饒陽太守盧全誠獨不從，思明等圍之。

translations.literal: Raoyang prefect Lu Quancheng alone did not submit, and Siming and the others besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: Only Raoyang prefect Lu Quancheng refused to yield, and Siming's forces laid siege to the city.

sentences.zh: 河間司法李奐將七千人、景城長史李□遣其子祀將八千人救之，皆為思明所敗。

translations.literal: Hejian judicial officer Li Huan led seven thousand men, and Jingcheng chief administrator Li □ sent his son Si with eight thousand men to rescue it; all were defeated by Siming.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan, judicial officer of Hejian, marched seven thousand men to the relief, and Li Min, chief administrator of Jingcheng, sent his son Si with eight thousand more—but Siming defeated them both.

sentences.zh: 上命郭子儀罷圍雲中，還朔方，益發兵進取東京；

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Guo Ziyi to cease the siege of Yunzhong, return to Shuofang, and further dispatch troops to advance and take the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Guo Ziyi to lift the siege of Yunzhong, return to Shuofang, and send more troops to retake the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 選良將一人分兵先出井陘，定河北。

translations.literal: Select one good general to divide troops and first go out through Jingxing Pass to settle Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He was to choose a capable general to lead a detached force through Jingxing Pass and pacify Hebei.

sentences.zh: 子儀薦李光弼，癸亥，以光弼為河東節度使，分朔方兵萬人與之。

translations.literal: Ziyi recommended Li Guangbi; on guihai Guangbi was made Hedong military commissioner, and ten thousand Shuofang troops were divided and given to him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi recommended Li Guangbi. On guihai Guangbi was appointed Hedong military commissioner and given ten thousand men from the Shuofang army.

sentences.zh: 甲子，加哥舒翰左僕射、同平章事，餘如故。

translations.literal: On jiazi Geshu Han was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Associate Grand Councillor; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Geshu Han was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Associate Grand Councillor; his other offices were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 置南陽節度使，以南陽太守魯炅為之，將嶺南、黔中、襄陽子弟五萬人屯葉北，以備安祿山。

translations.literal: The Nanyang military commission was established, with Nanyang prefect Lu Cong as commissioner, leading fifty thousand sons and younger brothers from Lingnan, Qianzhong, and Xiangyang to encamp north of Ye, to guard against An Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: A Nanyang military commission was created, with Nanyang prefect Lu Cong in command. He led fifty thousand recruits from Lingnan, Qianzhong, and Xiangyang to camp north of Ye and block An Lushan's advance.

sentences.zh: 炅表薛願為穎川太守兼防禦使，龐堅為副使。

translations.literal: Cong memorialized Xue Yuan as Yingchuan prefect concurrently defense commissioner, and Pang Jian as vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Cong recommended Xue Yuan as prefect of Yingchuan and defense commissioner, with Pang Jian as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 願，故太子瑛之妃兄；

translations.literal: Yuan was the elder brother of the former crown prince Ying's consort.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yuan was the elder brother of the former crown prince Ying's consort.

sentences.zh: 堅，玉之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Jian was Yu's great-great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Jian was the great-great-grandson of Pang Yu.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，安祿山遣其子慶緒寇潼關，哥舒翰擊卻之。

translations.literal: On yichou An Lushan sent his son Qingxu to raid Tong Pass; Geshu Han struck and repelled him.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou An Lushan sent his son Qingxu against Tong Pass; Geshu Han drove him back.

sentences.zh: 己巳，加顏真卿戶部侍郎兼本郡防禦使；

translations.literal: On jisi Yan Zhenqing was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue concurrently defense commissioner of his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi Yan Zhenqing was made Vice Minister of Revenue and defense commissioner of his own commandery.

sentences.zh: 真卿以李□為副。

translations.literal: Zhenqing made Li □ his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing appointed Li Min as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙戌，加李光弼魏郡太守、河北道採訪史。

translations.literal: In the second month, on bingxu, Li Guangbi was additionally made Wei commandery prefect and Hebei circuit investigating commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on bingxu, Li Guangbi was also made prefect of Wei commandery and investigating commissioner of the Hebei circuit.

sentences.zh: 史思明等圍饒陽二十九日，不下，李光弼將蕃、漢步騎萬餘人、太原弩手三千人出井陘。

translations.literal: Shi Siming and the others besieged Raoyang for twenty-nine days without taking it; Li Guangbi led more than ten thousand barbarian and Han infantry and cavalry and three thousand Taiyuan crossbowmen out through Jingxing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming had besieged Raoyang for twenty-nine days without success when Li Guangbi marched out of Jingxing Pass with more than ten thousand mixed foot and horse and three thousand Taiyuan crossbowmen.

sentences.zh: 己亥，至常山，常山團練兵三千人殺胡兵，執安思義出降。

translations.literal: On jihai he reached Changshan; three thousand Changshan militia killed the Hu troops, seized An Siyi, and came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai he reached Changshan, where three thousand local militiamen killed the rebel garrison, seized An Siyi, and surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 光弼謂思義曰：「汝自知當死否？」

translations.literal: Guangbi said to Siyi, 'Do you yourself know you ought to die?'
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi asked Siyi, 'Do you know you deserve death?'

sentences.zh: 思義不應。

translations.literal: Siyi did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Siyi said nothing.

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「汝久更陳行，視吾此眾，可敵思明否？

translations.literal: Guangbi said, 'You have long served in the ranks of battle—look at this host of mine; can it match Siming?
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said, 'You are a veteran of many campaigns—look at my army. Can it stand against Siming?

sentences.zh: 今為我計當如何？

translations.literal: Now devise a plan for me—what should be done?
translations.idiomatic: Tell me what you would do in my place.

sentences.zh: 汝策可取，當不殺汝。」

translations.literal: If your stratagem can be adopted, I shall not kill you.'
translations.idiomatic: Give me sound counsel, and I will spare your life.'

sentences.zh: 思義曰：「大夫士馬遠來疲弊，猝遇大敵，恐未易當；

translations.literal: Siyi said, 'Your Excellency's officers and horses have come from afar, weary and spent; suddenly meeting a great enemy, I fear they will not be easy to withstand.
translations.idiomatic: Siyi said, 'Your men and horses have marched a long way and are exhausted; if they meet the main rebel force suddenly, they may not hold.

sentences.zh: 不如移軍入城，早為備御，先料勝負，然後出兵。

translations.literal: Better to shift the army into the city, make preparations early, first reckon victory and defeat, and then send troops out.
translations.idiomatic: Better to withdraw into the city, fortify your position, weigh the odds, and only then give battle.

sentences.zh: 胡騎雖銳，不能持重，苟不獲利，氣沮心離，於時乃可圖矣。

translations.literal: Hu cavalry, though sharp, cannot sustain weight; if they do not gain profit, spirits will be damped and hearts will separate—at that time they can then be plotted against.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel horsemen are fierce but cannot sustain a long fight; if they gain nothing, their spirit will break and their ranks will scatter—then you can strike.

sentences.zh: 思明今在饒陽，去此不二百里。

translations.literal: Siming is now at Raoyang, not two hundred li from here.
translations.idiomatic: Siming is at Raoyang now, less than two hundred li away.

sentences.zh: 昨暮羽書已去，計其先鋒來晨必至，而大軍繼之，不可不留意也。」

translations.literal: Last evening urgent dispatches had already gone out; I reckon the vanguard will surely arrive tomorrow morning, with the great army following—this cannot be treated lightly.'
translations.idiomatic: He sent urgent dispatches last night; his vanguard will reach us by dawn tomorrow and the main body will follow. You must be ready.'

sentences.zh: 光弼悅，釋其縛，即移軍入城。

translations.literal: Guangbi was pleased, released his bonds, and at once shifted the army into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi was pleased, freed him, and immediately withdrew his army into the city.

sentences.zh: 史思明聞常山不守，立解饒陽之圍；

translations.literal: Shi Siming heard Changshan could not be held and at once lifted the siege of Raoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming learned that Changshan had fallen, he immediately abandoned the siege of Raoyang.

sentences.zh: 明日未旦，先鋒已至，思明等繼之，合二萬餘騎，直抵城下。

translations.literal: The next day before dawn the vanguard had already arrived; Siming and the others followed, totaling more than twenty thousand horsemen, and came straight to below the city.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn the next day the rebel vanguard was already at the walls; Siming followed with more than twenty thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 光弼遣步卒五千自東門出戰，賊守門不退。

translations.literal: Guangbi sent five thousand foot soldiers out through the east gate to battle; the rebels held the gate and did not retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi sent five thousand infantry out the east gate to fight, but the rebels held their ground at the gate.

sentences.zh: 光弼命五百弩於城上齊發射之，賊稍卻；

translations.literal: Guangbi ordered five hundred crossbows on the wall to shoot together; the rebels slightly withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi had five hundred crossbowmen on the wall fire together, and the rebels fell back a little.

sentences.zh: 乃出弩手千人分為四隊，使其矢發發相繼，賊不能當，斂軍道北。

translations.literal: Then he sent out one thousand crossbowmen divided into four teams, making their arrows issue in continuous succession; the rebels could not withstand it and gathered their army north along the road.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent out a thousand crossbowmen in four ranks, their volleys rolling on without pause until the rebels could not stand it and pulled back north along the road.

sentences.zh: 光弼出兵五千為槍城於道南，夾呼沱水而陳；

translations.literal: Guangbi sent out five thousand troops and made a spear-wall south of the road, deploying in formation flanking the Hutuo River.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi sent five thousand men to build a palisade south of the road and drew up his line along the Hutuo River.

sentences.zh: 賊數以騎兵搏戰，光弼之兵射之，人馬中矢者太半，乃退，小憩以俟步兵。

translations.literal: The rebels repeatedly sent cavalry to grapple in battle; Guangbi's troops shot at them, and more than half of men and horses were struck by arrows, whereupon they withdrew and rested briefly to await the infantry.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels charged again and again with cavalry, but Guangbi's archers cut them down until more than half of men and horses were hit; the rebels withdrew to rest and wait for their foot soldiers.

sentences.zh: 有村民告賊步兵五千自饒陽來，晝夜行百七十里，至九門南逢壁，度憩息。

translations.literal: A village man reported that five thousand rebel foot soldiers were coming from Raoyang, marching day and night one hundred seventy li, reaching Fengbi south of Jiumen, where they expected to rest.
translations.idiomatic: A villager reported that five thousand rebel infantry were hurrying from Raoyang—they had marched a hundred and seventy li without pause and were resting at Fengbi, south of Jiumen.

sentences.zh: 光弼遣步騎各二千，匿旗鼓，並水潛行，至逢壁，賊方飯，縱兵掩擊，殺之無遺。

translations.literal: Guangbi sent two thousand foot soldiers and two thousand cavalry each, hiding banners and drums, stealing along by the water; reaching Fengbi, the rebels were just eating, and he released troops for a surprise attack, killing them without remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi sent two thousand foot and two thousand horse, hiding their banners and drums and stealing along the riverbank. They reached Fengbi while the rebels were at their meal and fell on them, slaughtering every man.

sentences.zh: 思明聞之，失勢，退入九門。

translations.literal: Siming heard of it, lost momentum, and withdrew into Jiumen.
translations.idiomatic: When Siming heard the news, his force lost heart and he fell back into Jiumen.

sentences.zh: 時常山九縣，七附官軍，惟九門、蒿城為賊所據。

translations.literal: At the time, of Changshan's nine counties, seven attached to the official army; only Jiumen and Haocheng were held by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Of Changshan's nine counties, seven now stood with the imperial army; only Jiumen and Haocheng remained in rebel hands.

sentences.zh: 光弼遣裨將張奉璋以兵五百戍石邑，餘皆三百人戍之。

translations.literal: Guangbi sent lieutenant general Zhang Fengzhang with five hundred troops to garrison Shiyi; the rest were garrisoned with three hundred men each.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi posted lieutenant Zhang Fengzhang with five hundred men at Shiyi and stationed three hundred at each of the other counties.

sentences.zh: 上以吳王祗為靈昌太守、河南都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: The emperor made Prince Wu Zhi Lingchang prefect and Henan overall commander of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Prince Wu Zhi prefect of Lingchang and overall commander of Henan's military affairs.

sentences.zh: 賈賁前至雍丘，有眾二千。

translations.literal: Jia Ben had earlier reached Yongqiu and had a host of two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Ben had already reached Yongqiu with two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 先是譙郡太守楊萬石以郡降安祿山，逼真源令河東張巡使為長史，西迎賊。

translations.literal: Earlier Qiao commandery prefect Yang Wanshi had surrendered the commandery to An Lushan and, pressing Zhenyuan magistrate Zhang Xun of Hedong, made him chief administrator and sent him west to welcome the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Qiao commandery prefect Yang Wanshi had surrendered to An Lushan and forced Zhenyuan magistrate Zhang Xun of Hedong to serve as his chief administrator and march west to meet the rebels.

sentences.zh: 巡至真源，帥吏民哭於玄元皇帝廟，起兵討賊，吏民樂從者數千人；

translations.literal: When Xun reached Zhenyuan, he led officials and people to weep at the Temple of the Mysterious Prime Emperor, raised troops to punish the rebels, and officials and people gladly following numbered several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun reached Zhenyuan he led officials and commoners to weep before the Temple of the Mysterious Prime Emperor, then raised a force to fight the rebels; several thousand men rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 巡選精兵千人西至雍丘，與賈賁合。

translations.literal: Xun selected one thousand elite troops and went west to Yongqiu, joining with Jia Ben.
translations.idiomatic: Xun picked a thousand seasoned fighters and marched west to Yongqiu, where he joined Jia Ben.

sentences.zh: 初，雍丘令令狐潮以縣降賊，賊以為將，使東擊淮陽救兵於襄邑，破之，俘百餘人，拘於雍丘，將殺之，往見李庭望；

translations.literal: Earlier, Yongqiu magistrate Linghu Chao had surrendered the county to the rebels; the rebels made him a general and sent him east to strike Huaiyang relief troops at Xiangyi, defeated them, captured more than a hundred men, detained them at Yongqiu, and were about to kill them when he went to see Li Tingwang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yongqiu magistrate Linghu Chao had surrendered his county to the rebels and been made a general. Sent east to intercept Huaiyang relief troops at Xiangyi, he routed them, took more than a hundred prisoners back to Yongqiu, and was about to execute them when he went to see Li Tingwang.

sentences.zh: 淮陽兵遂殺守者，潮棄妻子走，故賈賁得以其間入雍丘。

translations.literal: The Huaiyang troops then killed the guards; Chao abandoned wife and children and fled, and so Jia Ben was able in that interval to enter Yongqiu.
translations.idiomatic: The Huaiyang prisoners killed their guards; Chao abandoned his family and fled, and in that opening Jia Ben slipped into Yongqiu.

sentences.zh: 庚子，潮引賊精兵攻雍丘；

translations.literal: On gengzi Chao led rebel elite troops to attack Yongqiu.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Chao returned with rebel crack troops to assault Yongqiu.

sentences.zh: 賁出戰，敗死。

translations.literal: Ben went out to battle, was defeated, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Ben went out to fight, was defeated, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 張巡力戰卻賊，因兼領賁眾，自稱吳王先鋒使。

translations.literal: Zhang Xun fought fiercely and repelled the rebels, then concurrently took command of Ben's host and styled himself vanguard commissioner of Prince Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun fought hard and drove the rebels back, took command of Ben's men, and styled himself vanguard commissioner of Prince Wu.

sentences.zh: 三月，乙卯，潮復與賊將李懷仙、楊朝宗、謝元同等四萬餘眾奄至城下；

translations.literal: In the third month, on yimao, Chao again with rebel generals Li Huaixian, Yang Chaozong, Xie Yuantong, and the like brought more than forty thousand troops and suddenly arrived below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on yimao, Chao returned with rebel generals Li Huaixian, Yang Chaozong, Xie Yuantong, and others, more than forty thousand men in all, and suddenly appeared before the city.

sentences.zh: 眾懼，莫有固志。

translations.literal: The host feared; none had firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: The men were terrified, and morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 巡曰：「賊兵精銳，有輕我心。

translations.literal: Xun said, "The rebel troops are elite and sharp; they hold our hearts lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Xun said, "The rebels are crack troops—they think little of us.

sentences.zh: 今出其不意擊之，彼必驚潰。

translations.literal: Now strike them by surprise; they will surely be startled and routed.
translations.idiomatic: If we hit them where they do not expect it, they will panic and break.

sentences.zh: 賊勢小折，然後城可守也。」

translations.literal: When the rebels' momentum is slightly broken, then the city can be held."
translations.idiomatic: Once we blunt their attack, the city can be held."

sentences.zh: 乃使千人乘城；

translations.literal: He then had one thousand men man the walls.
translations.idiomatic: He then posted a thousand men on the walls.

sentences.zh: 自帥千人，分數隊，開門突出。

translations.literal: Himself leading one thousand men, divided into several companies, he opened the gates and burst out.
translations.idiomatic: He personally led a thousand men in several squads and sallied out through the gates.

sentences.zh: 巡身先士卒，直衝賊陳，人馬辟易，賊遂退。

translations.literal: Xun took the lead before officers and men, charging straight into the rebel formation; men and horses gave way, and the rebels then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xun led from the front, drove straight into the rebel line, and men and horses scattered before him; the rebels fell back.

sentences.zh: 明日，復進攻城，設百砲環城，樓堞皆盡；

translations.literal: The next day they again advanced to attack the city, setting up a hundred trebuchets encircling the wall; towers and battlements were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the rebels returned and assaulted the walls, ringing the city with a hundred catapults until every tower and battlement was smashed.

sentences.zh: 巡於城上立木柵以拒之。

translations.literal: Xun erected wooden palisades atop the wall to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Xun put up wooden barricades on the ramparts to hold them off.

sentences.zh: 賊蟻附而登，巡束蒿灌脂，焚而投之，賊不得上。

translations.literal: The rebels climbed like ants attaching themselves; Xun bound reeds, soaked them in grease, burned them and cast them down—the rebels could not ascend.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels swarmed up the walls like ants; Xun bound reeds, soaked them in oil, set them ablaze, and hurled them down, and the rebels could not climb.

sentences.zh: 時同賊隙，出兵擊之，或夜縋斫營。

translations.literal: Whenever there was an opening with the rebels, troops went out to strike them, or at night were lowered by rope to cut at their camps.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an opening appeared, he sent troops against them, and at night men were lowered by rope to raid their camps.

sentences.zh: 積六十餘日，大小三百餘戰，帶甲而食，裹瘡復戰，賊遂敗走。

translations.literal: Over sixty-plus days accumulated, three hundred-odd engagements large and small; they ate in armor, bound wounds and fought again, and the rebels then were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: After more than sixty days and over three hundred battles, eating in armor and fighting on with bound wounds, the rebels were finally driven off.

sentences.zh: 巡乘勝追之，獲胡兵二千人而還，軍聲大振。

translations.literal: Xun pursued them on the victory, captured two thousand Hu troops and returned; the army's reputation greatly swelled.
translations.idiomatic: Xun pressed the pursuit, took two thousand foreign troops prisoner, and returned; his army's fame soared.

sentences.zh: 初，戶部尚書安思順知祿山反謀，因入朝奏之。

translations.literal: Initially, Minister of Revenue An Sishun knew of Lushan's rebellion plot and therefore entered court to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Minister of Revenue An Sishun had learned of An Lushan's plot to rebel and reported it when he came to court.

sentences.zh: 及祿山反，上以思順先奏，不之罪也。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, the emperor, because Sishun had reported first, did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled, the emperor held that Sishun had warned him first and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 哥舒翰素與之有隙，使人詐為祿山遺思順書，於關門擒之以獻，且數思順七罪，請誅之。

translations.literal: Geshu Han had long had a rift with him; he sent a man to forge a letter from Lushan to Sishun, seized him at Tong Pass and presented him, and also enumerated seven crimes of Sishun, requesting execution.
translations.idiomatic: Geshu Han had long borne a grudge against him. He had a man forge a letter from Lushan to Sishun, seized Sishun at Tong Pass and handed him over, listed seven charges against him, and asked that he be put to death.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，思順及弟太僕卿元貞皆坐死，家屬徙嶺外。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Sishun and his younger brother Grand Master of the Stud Yuanzhen were both punished with death; their families were exiled beyond the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Sishun and his brother Yuanzhen, Grand Master of the Stud, were executed, and their families were sent into exile beyond the Ling.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠不能救，由是始畏翰。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong could not save them; from this he began to fear Han.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong was unable to save them, and from that time he began to fear Geshu Han.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀至朔方，益選精兵，戊午，進軍於代。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi reached Shuofang, further selected elite troops; on wuwu, he advanced the army to Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi reached Shuofang, picked more crack troops, and on wuwu marched toward Dai.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，吳王祗擊謝元同，走之，拜陳留太守、河南節度使。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Prince Wu Zhi attacked Xie Yuantong, drove him off, and was appointed Chenliu prefect and Henan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Prince Wu Zhi routed Xie Yuantong and was made prefect of Chenliu and military commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以河東節度使李光弼為范陽長史、河北節度使，加顏真卿河北採訪使。

translations.literal: On renwu, Hedong military commissioner Li Guangbi was made Fanyang chief administrator and Hebei military commissioner; Yan Zhenqing was additionally made Hebei investigating commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Li Guangbi, Hedong military commissioner, was made chief administrator of Fanyang and military commissioner of Hebei, and Yan Zhenqing was also made investigating commissioner for Hebei.

sentences.zh: 真卿以張澹為支使。

translations.literal: Zhenqing made Zhang Dan an aide commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing appointed Zhang Dan as his aide commissioner.

sentences.zh: 先是清河客李萼，年二十餘，為郡人乞師於真卿曰：「公首唱大義，河北諸郡恃公以為長城。

translations.literal: Earlier, a Qinghe guest Li E, aged twenty-plus, on behalf of the commandery's people begged troops from Zhenqing, saying, "Your Excellency first raised the great cause; the Hebei commanderies rely on you as their Great Wall.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a visitor to Qinghe named Li E, just over twenty, had come on the county's behalf to ask Zhenqing for troops. He said, "Your Excellency was the first to raise the banner of loyalty; every commandery in Hebei looks to you as its bulwark.

sentences.zh: 今清河，公之西鄰，國家平日聚江、淮、河南錢帛於彼以贍北軍，謂之『天下北庫』；

translations.literal: Now Qinghe is Your Excellency's western neighbor; the state in ordinary times gathered Jiang, Huai, and Henan money and silks there to supply the northern armies—it was called the 'Northern Storehouse of the Realm.'
translations.idiomatic: Qinghe lies just west of you. In peacetime the court stored the revenue of the Jiang, Huai, and Henan regions there to supply the northern armies—it was called the 'Northern Storehouse of the Realm.'

sentences.zh: 今有布三百餘萬匹，帛八十餘萬匹，錢三十餘萬緡，糧三十餘萬斛。

translations.literal: Now there are more than three million bolts of cloth, more than eight hundred thousand bolts of silk, more than three hundred thousand strings of cash, and more than three hundred thousand piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: It now holds more than three million bolts of cloth, eight hundred thousand bolts of silk, three hundred thousand strings of cash, and three hundred thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 昔討默啜，甲兵皆貯清河庫，今有五十餘萬事；

translations.literal: Formerly in campaigning against Mohechuo, armor and weapons were all stored in the Qinghe depot; now there are more than five hundred thousand pieces.
translations.idiomatic: When the court campaigned against Mohechuo, arms and armor were stored in Qinghe's depots; more than five hundred thousand pieces remain there now.

sentences.zh: 戶七萬，口十餘萬。

translations.literal: Households seventy thousand, mouths one hundred thousand-plus.
translations.idiomatic: There are seventy thousand households and more than one hundred thousand people.

sentences.zh: 竊計財足以三平原之富，兵足以倍平原之強。

translations.literal: I venture to reckon that its wealth suffices for three times Pingyuan commandery's riches, and its troops suffice to double Pingyuan commandery's strength.
translations.idiomatic: By my reckoning, its wealth is triple that of Pingyuan, and its armed strength twice as great.

sentences.zh: 公誠資以士卒，撫而有之，以二郡為腹心，則餘郡如四支，無不隨所使矣。」

translations.literal: If Your Excellency truly supplies troops and pacifies and holds it, taking the two commanderies as heart and belly, then the remaining commanderies will be like the four limbs—none will fail to follow wherever sent."
translations.idiomatic: If you supply troops and take both counties as your core, the rest of Hebei will follow like limbs on a body—every county will do your bidding."

sentences.zh: 真卿曰：「平原兵新集，尚未訓練，自保恐不足，何暇及鄰！

translations.literal: Zhenqing said, "Pingyuan's troops are newly gathered and not yet trained; self-defense probably is insufficient—how have we leisure to reach neighbors!
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing replied, "My forces at Pingyuan are newly raised and barely trained. I can scarcely defend myself—how can I spare troops for a neighbor?

sentences.zh: 雖然，借若諾子之請，則將何為乎？」

translations.literal: Even so, if I were to grant your request, what then would you do?"
translations.idiomatic: Even so, if I agreed to your request—what would you do?"

sentences.zh: 萼曰：「清河遣僕銜命於公者，非力不足而借公之師以嘗寇也，亦欲觀大賢之明義耳。

translations.literal: E said, "That Qinghe sent me bearing commission to Your Excellency was not because strength was insufficient and we borrowed Your Excellency's army to test the rebels; it was also to observe a great worthy's clear righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Li E said, "Qinghe did not send me because we lacked strength and needed your troops to probe the enemy. We wanted to see whether a man of your stature would act on principle.

sentences.zh: 今仰瞻高意，未有決辭定色，僕何敢遽言所為哉！」

translations.literal: Now looking up to Your Excellency's lofty intent, there is no decisive words or settled expression—how dare I hastily speak of what is to be done!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet I look to you now and find no firm word or clear intent—how dare I speak of my plan before you commit?"

sentences.zh: 真卿奇之，欲與之兵。

translations.literal: Zhenqing marveled at him and wished to give him troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing was impressed and wanted to lend him troops.

sentences.zh: 眾以為萼年少輕虜，徒分兵力，必無所成，真卿不得已辭之。

translations.literal: The company thought E was young and belittled the rebels, that dividing military strength would be in vain and there would certainly be no achievement; Zhenqing had no choice but to decline.
translations.idiomatic: His staff thought Li E too young and too dismissive of the enemy; splitting their strength would achieve nothing. Zhenqing reluctantly refused.

sentences.zh: 萼就館，復為書說真卿，以為：「清河去逆效順，奉粟帛器械以資軍，公乃不納而疑之。

translations.literal: E went to his lodgings and again wrote to persuade Zhenqing, stating, "Qinghe turned from rebellion to loyalty and presented grain, silk, and equipment to supply the army, yet Your Excellency did not accept but instead harbored suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Li E went to his lodgings and wrote again, arguing that "Qinghe had turned against the rebels and offered grain, silk, and weapons to support the cause—and yet Zhenqing had not only refused but treated them with suspicion.

sentences.zh: 僕回轅之後，清河不能孤立，必有所繫托，將為公西面之強敵，公能無悔乎？」

translations.literal: After I turn my carriage back, Qinghe cannot stand alone and must attach itself somewhere; it will become a strong enemy on Your Excellency's western flank—can Your Excellency be without regret?"
translations.idiomatic: Once I return, Qinghe cannot stand alone. It will have to seek another patron—and become a formidable enemy on your western flank. Will you not regret this?"

sentences.zh: 真卿大驚，遽詣其館，以兵六千借之；

translations.literal: Zhenqing was greatly startled, hastily went to his lodgings, and lent him six thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Zhenqing hurried to his lodgings and lent him six thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 送至境，執手別。

translations.literal: He saw him to the border, clasped hands, and parted.
translations.idiomatic: He escorted Li E to the border and parted with a handclasp.

sentences.zh: 真卿問曰：「兵已行矣，可以言子之所為乎？」

translations.literal: Zhenqing asked, "The troops have already marched—may I now hear what you intend to do?"
translations.idiomatic: As they were leaving, Zhenqing asked, "Now that the troops are on their way—may I hear your plan?"

sentences.zh: 萼曰：「聞朝廷遣程千里將精兵十萬出崞口討賊，賊據險拒之，不得前。

translations.literal: E said, "I hear the court sent Cheng Qianli leading one hundred thousand elite troops out through Gu Pass to punish the rebels; the rebels held the narrow passes and blocked them, and they could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Li E said, "I hear the court has sent Cheng Qianli with one hundred thousand elite troops through Gu Pass against the rebels, but the rebels hold the passes and he cannot get through.

sentences.zh: 今當引兵先擊魏郡，執祿山所署太守袁之泰，納舊太守司馬垂，使為西南主人；

translations.literal: Now we should lead troops first to strike Wei commandery, seize Lushan's appointed prefect Yuan Zhita, restore the former prefect Sima Chui, and make him host on the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: I plan to strike Wei commandery first, seize Yuan Zhita, the prefect An Lushan appointed, restore the old prefect Sima Chui, and make him our base on the southwest.

sentences.zh: 分兵開崞口，出千里之師，因討汲、鄴以北至於幽陵郡縣之未下者；

translations.literal: Divide troops to open Gu Pass, release Qianli's army, and thereby punish Ji, Ye, and northward to Youling commanderies and counties not yet taken.
translations.idiomatic: Then split our force to open Gu Pass and unleash Cheng Qianli's army, and sweep north from Ji and Ye through every county as far as Youling that still holds out.

sentences.zh: 平原、清河帥諸同盟，合兵十萬，南臨孟津，分兵循河，據守要害，制其北走之路。

translations.literal: Pingyuan and Qinghe will lead the allied leagues, combine forces of one hundred thousand, face south on Meng Ford, divide troops along the river, hold key points, and control their route of flight north.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyuan and Qinghe will lead the allied forces—one hundred thousand men—to the Meng Ford, with detachments along the Yellow River holding the key crossings and cutting off any northern retreat.

sentences.zh: 計官軍東討者不下二十萬，河南義兵西向者亦不減十萬。

translations.literal: Counting imperial troops campaigning east, not less than two hundred thousand; Henan loyalist troops facing west also not less than one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Between imperial armies marching east and Henan loyalists facing west, there will be at least three hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 公但當表朝廷堅壁勿戰，不過月餘，賊必有內潰相圖之變矣。」

translations.literal: Your Excellency need only memorialize the court to hold fast behind walls and not fight; within a month or so the rebels will certainly have internal collapse and mutual plotting against one another."
translations.idiomatic: You need only urge the court to stand on the defensive. Within a month the rebels will turn on one another."

sentences.zh: 真卿曰「善！」

translations.literal: Zhenqing said, "Excellent!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing said, "Excellent!"

sentences.zh: 命錄事參軍李擇交及平原令范冬馥將其兵，會清河兵四千及博平兵千人軍於堂邑西南。

translations.literal: He ordered recorder-assistant Li Zejiao and Pingyuan magistrate Fan Dongfu to lead his troops; they joined Qinghe's four thousand troops and Boping's one thousand troops and encamped southwest of Tangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Li Zejiao, his recorder-assistant, and Fan Dongfu, magistrate of Pingyuan, to lead the force; they joined four thousand Qinghe troops and one thousand from Boping and encamped southwest of Tangyi.

sentences.zh: 袁知泰遣其將白嗣恭等將二萬餘人來逆戰，三郡兵力戰盡日，魏兵大敗，斬首萬餘級，捕虜千餘人，得馬千匹，軍資甚眾，知泰奔汲郡。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhita sent his generals Bai Sigong and others leading more than twenty thousand men to meet in battle; the three commanderies' troops fought fiercely all day; Wei troops were greatly defeated—heads cut more than ten thousand, captives more than one thousand, horses obtained one thousand; military supplies were very numerous; Zhita fled to Ji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhita sent his generals Bai Sigong and others with more than twenty thousand men to meet them. The armies of the three counties fought all day; the Wei force was routed—more than ten thousand heads taken, more than a thousand prisoners, a thousand horses captured, and vast stores of supplies. Zhita fled to Ji commandery.

sentences.zh: 遂克魏郡，軍聲大振。

translations.literal: They then took Wei commandery; the army's reputation greatly swelled.
translations.idiomatic: They took Wei commandery, and their fame spread far.

sentences.zh: 時北海太守賀蘭進明亦起兵，真卿以書召之並力，進明將步騎五千渡河，真卿陳兵逆之，相揖，哭於馬上，哀動行伍。

translations.literal: At that time Beihai prefect Helan Jinming also raised troops; Zhenqing summoned him by letter to join forces; Jinming led five thousand infantry and cavalry across the river; Zhenqing deployed troops to meet him; they bowed to each other, wept on horseback—the grief moved the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Beihai prefect Helan Jinming had also raised troops. Zhenqing summoned him by letter to join forces. Jinming crossed the river with five thousand foot and horse. Zhenqing lined up his men to meet him; they bowed to each other and wept on horseback until the whole column was moved.

sentences.zh: 進明屯平原城南，休養士馬，真卿每事咨之，由是軍權稍移於進明矣，真卿不以為嫌。

translations.literal: Jinming encamped south of Pingyuan city, rested troops and horses; Zhenqing consulted him on every matter—thus military authority gradually shifted to Jinming; Zhenqing did not regard it as offense.
translations.idiomatic: Jinming camped south of Pingyuan city and rested his men. Zhenqing consulted him on every decision, and military authority gradually shifted to Jinming—but Zhenqing held no grudge.

sentences.zh: 真卿以堂邑之功讓進明，進明奏其狀，取捨任意。

translations.literal: Zhenqing yielded to Jinming the credit for Tangyi; Jinming reported the facts and took or discarded as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing gave Jinming credit for the victory at Tangyi. Jinming reported to the throne and doled out rewards as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 敕加進明河北招討使，擇交、冬馥微進資級，清河、博平有功者皆不錄。

translations.literal: An edict additionally made Jinming Hebei recruiting-and-punishing commissioner; Zejiao and Dongfu received slight promotion in rank; Qinghe and Boping men with merit were all unrecorded.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Jinming commissioner for recruiting and punishing in Hebei. Zejiao and Dongfu received modest promotions; the men of Qinghe and Boping who had fought were passed over entirely.

sentences.zh: 進明攻信都郡，久之，不克；

translations.literal: Jinming attacked Xindu commandery; after a long time, he could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Jinming besieged Xindu commandery for a long time without success.

sentences.zh: 錄事參軍長安第五琦勸進明厚以金帛募勇士，遂克之。

translations.literal: Recorder-assistant of Chang'an Diwu Qi advised Jinming to lavishly use gold and silks to recruit brave warriors; he then took it.
translations.idiomatic: His recorder-assistant, Diwu Qi of Chang'an, urged Jinming to offer gold and silk to recruit fierce fighters—and Xindu fell.

sentences.zh: 李光弼與史思明相守四十餘日，思明絕常山糧道。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi and Shi Siming faced each other for forty-odd days; Siming cut off Changshan's grain routes.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi and Shi Siming had faced each other for more than forty days when Siming cut Changshan's supply lines.

sentences.zh: 城中乏草，馬食薦籍。

translations.literal: Inside the city there was lack of fodder; horses ate matting.
translations.idiomatic: Fodder ran short inside the city, and the horses ate bedding straw.

sentences.zh: 光弼以車五百乘之石邑取草，將車者皆衣甲，弩手千人衛之，為方陳而行，賊不能奪。

translations.literal: Guangbi used five hundred carts to go to Shiyi for fodder; cart drivers all wore armor, one thousand crossbowmen guarded them, advancing in square formation—the rebels could not seize them.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi sent five hundred carts to Shiyi for fodder. The drivers wore armor, a thousand crossbowmen escorted them in square formation, and the rebels could not intercept them.

sentences.zh: 蔡希德引兵攻石邑，張奉璋拒卻之。

translations.literal: Cai Xide led troops to attack Shiyi; Zhang Fengzhang repelled him.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xide attacked Shiyi, but Zhang Fengzhang drove him off.

sentences.zh: 光弼遣使告急於郭子儀，子儀引兵自井陘出，夏，四月，壬辰，至常山，與光弼合，蕃、漢步騎共十餘萬。

translations.literal: Guangbi sent envoys urgently to report to Guo Ziyi; Ziyi led troops out through Jingxing Pass—in summer, fourth month, on renchen, reaching Changshan, joining with Guangbi—barbarian and Han infantry and cavalry together more than one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi sent an urgent appeal to Guo Ziyi. Ziyi marched out of Jingxing Pass; in summer, the fourth month, on renchen he reached Changshan and joined Guangbi—more than one hundred thousand mixed foot and horse between them.

sentences.zh: 甲午，子儀、光弼與史思明等戰於九門城南，思明大敗。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Ziyi, Guangbi, and Shi Siming and the others fought south of Jiumen city; Siming was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Guo Ziyi and Li Guangbi met Shi Siming and the others south of Jiumen city and crushed them.

sentences.zh: 中郎將渾瑊射李立節，殺之。

translations.literal: Palace-guard general Hun Jian shot Li Lijie and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Guard General Hun Jian shot Li Lijie dead.

sentences.zh: 瑊，釋之之子也。

translations.literal: Jian was the son of Shizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was the son of Hun Shizhi.

sentences.zh: 思明收餘眾奔趙郡，蔡希德奔鉅鹿。

translations.literal: Siming gathered remnant troops and fled to Zhao commandery; Cai Xide fled to Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Siming rallied his remnants and fled to Zhao commandery; Cai Xide fled to Julu.

sentences.zh: 思明自趙郡如博陵，時博陵已降官軍，思明盡殺郡官。

translations.literal: Siming from Zhao commandery went to Boling; at that time Boling had already surrendered to the imperial army; Siming killed all commandery officials.
translations.idiomatic: Siming went from Zhao commandery toward Boling, which had already surrendered to the imperial army. He slaughtered every official in the county.

sentences.zh: 河朔之民苦賊殘暴，所在屯結，多至二萬人，少者萬人，各為營以拒賊；

translations.literal: The people of Heshuo suffered under the rebels' cruel violence; everywhere they gathered and formed groups—many up to twenty thousand, few ten thousand—each making camps to resist the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Heshuo, ground down by rebel brutality, had banded together everywhere—some twenty thousand strong, others ten thousand—and built camps to resist the rebels.

sentences.zh: 及郭、李軍至，爭出自效。

translations.literal: When Guo and Li's armies arrived, they vied to come forward and serve.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Ziyi and Li Guangbi arrived, they all rushed to serve.

sentences.zh: 庚子，攻趙郡；

translations.literal: On gengzi, they attacked Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi they attacked Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 一日，城降。

translations.literal: In one day, the city surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell in a single day.

sentences.zh: 士卒多虜掠，光弼坐城門，收所獲，悉歸之，民大悅。

translations.literal: Troops mostly plundered captives; Guangbi sat at the city gate, collected what was taken, entirely returned it—the people greatly rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers had looted heavily. Guangbi sat at the city gate, collected everything they had taken, and returned it all—the people were overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 子儀生擒四千人，皆捨之，斬祿山太守郭獻璆。

translations.literal: Ziyi alive-captured four thousand men, all released; beheaded Lushan's prefect Guo Xianqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi took four thousand prisoners alive and released them all, but executed Guo Xianqiu, the prefect An Lushan had appointed.

sentences.zh: 光弼進圍博陵，十日，不拔，引兵還恆陽就食。

translations.literal: Guangbi advanced to besiege Boling; ten days, could not take it; led troops back to Hengyang for provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi moved on to besiege Boling, but after ten days could not take it and withdrew to Hengyang for supplies.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠問士之可為將者於左拾遺博平張鎬及蕭昕，鎬、昕薦左贊善大夫永壽來瑱。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong asked about men who could serve as generals of Left Remonstrance Boping Zhang Hao and Xiao Xin; Hao and Xin recommended Left Palace Companion Yongshou Lai Tian.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong asked Left Remonstrance Zhang Hao of Boping and Xiao Xin to name men fit for command. They recommended Left Palace Companion Lai Tian of Yongshou.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以瑱為穎川太守。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Tian was made Yingchuan prefect.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Lai Tian was made prefect of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 賊屢攻之，瑱前後破賊甚眾，加本郡防禦使，人謂之「來嚼鐵」。

translations.literal: The rebels repeatedly attacked him; Tian before and after defeated rebels in great numbers; he was additionally made the commandery's defense commissioner; people called him "Lai Chews Iron."
translations.idiomatic: Rebels attacked him again and again; Lai Tian defeated them repeatedly in large numbers. He was made defense commissioner of his commandery, and people called him "Lai Chews Iron."

sentences.zh: 安祿山使平盧節度使呂知誨誘安東副大都護馬靈察，殺之。

translations.literal: An Lushan sent Pinglu military commissioner Lü Zhihui to entice Andong deputy grand protect general Ma Lingcha and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan sent Pinglu military commissioner Lü Zhihui to lure Andong deputy grand protector Ma Lingcha to his death.

sentences.zh: 平盧游弈使武陟劉客奴、先鋒使董秦及安東將王玄志同謀討誅知誨，遣使逾海與顏真卿相聞，請取范陽以自效。

translations.literal: Pinglu roving commissioner Wuzhi Liu Kenú, vanguard commissioner Dong Qin, and Andong general Wang Xuanzhi together plotted to punish and kill Zhihui; they sent envoys across the sea to communicate with Yan Zhenqing, requesting to take Fanyang to prove their worth.
translations.idiomatic: Pinglu roving commissioner Liu Kenú of Wuzhi, vanguard commissioner Dong Qin, and Andong general Wang Xuanzhi plotted together to kill Zhihui. They sent messengers across the sea to Yan Zhenqing, offering to seize Fanyang in the court's service.

sentences.zh: 真卿遣判官賈載繼糧及戰士衣助之。

translations.literal: Zhenqing sent aide-administrator Jia Zai to follow with grain and soldiers' clothing to assist them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing sent his aide-administrator Jia Zai after them with grain and clothing for the troops.

sentences.zh: 真卿時惟一子頗，才十餘歲，使詣客奴為質。

translations.literal: Zhenqing at the time had only one son, Po, just ten-plus years old; he sent him to Kenú as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing had only one son, Po, barely in his teens; he sent the boy to Kenú as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞之，以客奴為平盧節度使，賜名正臣；

translations.literal: The court on hearing this made Kenú Pinglu military commissioner and bestowed the name Zhengchen.
translations.idiomatic: When the court learned of this, it made Kenú Pinglu military commissioner and gave him the name Zhengchen.

sentences.zh: 玄志為安東副大都護，董秦為平盧兵馬使。

translations.literal: Xuanzhi was made Andong deputy grand protect general; Dong Qin was made Pinglu army and horse commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanzhi was made Andong deputy grand protector, and Dong Qin Pinglu army commissioner.

sentences.zh: 南陽節度使魯炅立柵於滍水之南，安祿山將武令珣、畢思琛攻之。

translations.literal: Nanyang military commissioner Lu Gui established palisades south of the Zhi River; An Lushan's generals Wu Lingxun and Bi Sichen attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: Nanyang military commissioner Lu Gui built a fortified camp south of the Zhi River. An Lushan's generals Wu Lingxun and Bi Sichen attacked it.
